# Claude Fable 5.2

## Anthropic — Claude Fable 5.2

## Model Details

Claude Fable 5.2 is Anthropic's frontier model for technical work, setting a new bar in coding, finance, and the sciences. Fable 5.2 takes on ambiguous problems for days, questions and verifies its own work, and orchestrates subagents to optimize results in a loop.

- Model launch date: November 9, 2026
- EOL no sooner than: November 9, 2027
- Legacy period: 6 months
- Model lifecycle policy: Model lifecycle
- Model EOL date: N/A
- End User License Agreements and Terms of Use: View
- Model lifecycle: Active
- Context window: 1M tokens
- Max output tokens: 128K
- Sampling parameters: temperature must be 1.0 or unset; top_p must be 0.99 or unset; temperature and top_p cannot be specified together; top_k is not supported
- Reasoning: Supported (adaptive thinking is always on and cannot be disabled; effort level configurable — low, medium, high, xhigh, max; default: high) See Adaptive thinking.
- Preserved thinking: Thinking blocks are bound to the model and the conversation prefix that produced them. Replay earlier turns unchanged, or a request returns a 400 error. For more information, see Preserved thinking.
- Knowledge cutoff: June 2026

## Content Restrictions

Claude Fable 5.2 includes safety classifiers that block high-risk cybersecurity activities and most research biology tasks. When a classifier blocks a request, the API returns a standard HTTP 200 response withstop_reason: "refusal" and a stop_details object containing the restriction category. Organizations working in these areas can apply for less restrictive access through Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program and Life Sciences Verification Program.

Customers should handlestop_reason: "refusal" as a primary response path. Whether a refused request is billed depends on its category and on whether output had started. For details, see Billing notes.

Fallback credit for refused requests (beta)

When Claude Fable 5.2 refuses a request, the response can include a fallback credit token. Redeem the token when you retry the same request on a fallback model, and the retry is billed for the cached conversation prefix at cache-read rates instead of cache-write rates. Not every refusal carries a token. For more information, see Fallback credit for refused requests (beta).

Anthropic.title: Glossary
Anthropic.description: The Claude API does not currently offer fine-tuning, but ask your Anthropic contact if you are interested in exploring this option. ... Claude, an AI assistant for life and work built by Anthropic, is based on a large language model that has been fine-tuned and trained using RLHF.
Anthropic.content:
# Glossary

## Context window

The “context window” refers to the amount of text a language model can look back on and reference when generating new text. This is different from the large corpus of data the language model was trained on, and instead represents a “working memory” for the model. A larger context window allows the model to process and respond to more complex and lengthy prompts, whereas a smaller context window might limit the model’s ability to handle longer prompts or maintain coherence over extended conversations.

See the guide to understanding context windows to learn more.

## Fine-tuning

Fine-tuning is the process of further training a pretrained language model using additional data. This causes the model to start representing and mimicking the patterns and characteristics of the fine-tuning dataset. Claude is not a bare language model; it has already been fine-tuned to be a helpful assistant. The Claude API does not currently offer fine-tuning, but ask your Anthropic contact if you are interested in exploring this option. Fine-tuning can be useful for adapting a language model to a specific domain, task, or writing style, but it requires careful consideration of the fine-tuning data and the potential impact on the model’s performance and biases.

## HHH

HHH (helpful, honest, harmless) is a research framework that informs how Claude is trained to be beneficial to society. It is distinct from the Claude product tagline, “AI assistant for life and work.”

- A helpful AI will attempt to perform the task or answer the question posed to the best of its abilities, providing relevant and useful information.
- An honest AI will give accurate information, and not hallucinate or confabulate. It will acknowledge its limitations and uncertainties when appropriate.
- A harmless AI will not be offensive or discriminatory, and when asked to aid in a dangerous or unethical act, the AI should politely refuse and explain why it cannot comply.

## Latency

Latency, in the context of generative AI and large language models, refers to the time it takes for the model to respond to a given prompt. It is the delay between submitting a prompt and receiving the generated output. Lower latency indicates faster response times, which is crucial for real-time applications, chatbots, and interactive experiences. Factors that can affect latency include model size, hardware capabilities, network conditions, and the complexity of the prompt and the generated response.

## LLM

Large language models (LLMs) are AI language models with many parameters that are capable of performing a variety of surprisingly useful tasks. These models are trained on vast amounts of text data and can generate human-like text, answer questions, summarize information, and more. Claude, an AI assistant for life and work built by Anthropic, is based on a large language model that has been fine-tuned and trained using RLHF.

## MCP (Model Context Protocol)

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to LLMs. Like a USB-C port for AI applications, MCP provides a unified way to connect AI models to different data sources and tools. MCP allows AI systems to maintain consistent context across interactions and access external resources in a standardized manner. See the MCP documentation to learn more.

## MCP connector

The MCP connector is a feature that allows API users to connect to MCP servers directly from the Messages API without building an MCP client. This allows seamless integration with MCP-compatible tools and services through the Claude API. The MCP connector supports features such as tool calling and is available in beta. See the MCP connector documentation to learn more.

## Pretraining

Pretraining is the initial process of training language models on a large unlabeled corpus of text. In Claude’s case, autoregressive language models (such as Claude’s underlying model) are pretrained to predict the next word, given the previous context of text in the document. These pretrained models are not inherently good at answering questions or following instructions, and often require deep skill in prompt engineering to elicit the behaviors you want. Fine-tuning and RLHF are used to refine these pretrained models, making them more useful for a wide range of tasks.

## RAG (retrieval augmented generation)

Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that combines information retrieval with language model generation to improve the accuracy and relevance of the generated text, and to better ground the model’s response in evidence. In RAG, a language model is augmented with an external knowledge base or a set of documents that is passed into the context window. The data is retrieved at runtime when a query is sent to the model, although the model itself does not necessarily retrieve the data (but can with tool use and a retrieval function). When generating text, relevant information first must be retrieved from the knowledge base based on the input prompt, and then passed to the model along with the original query. The model uses this information to guide the output it generates. This allows the model to access and use information beyond its training data, reducing the reliance on memorization and improving the factual accuracy of the generated text. RAG can be particularly useful for tasks that require up-to-date information, domain-specific knowledge, or explicit citation of sources. However, the effectiveness of RAG depends on the quality and relevance of the external knowledge base and the knowledge that is retrieved at runtime.

## RLHF

Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is a technique used to train a pretrained language model to behave in ways that are consistent with human preferences. This can include helping the model follow instructions more effectively or act more like a chatbot. Human feedback consists of ranking a set of two or more example texts, and the reinforcement learning process encourages the model to prefer outputs that are similar to the higher-ranked ones. Claude has been trained using RLHF to be a more helpful assistant. For more details, you can read Anthropic’s paper on RLHF.

## Temperature

Temperature is a parameter that controls the randomness of a model’s predictions during text generation. Higher temperatures lead to more creative and diverse outputs, allowing for multiple variations in phrasing and, in the case of fiction, variation in answers as well. Lower temperatures result in more conservative and deterministic outputs that stick to the most probable phrasing and answers. Adjusting the temperature allows users to encourage a language model to explore rare, uncommon, or surprising word choices and sequences, rather than only selecting the most likely predictions.

Users might encounter non-determinism in APIs. Even with temperature set to 0, the results will not be fully deterministic, and identical inputs might produce different outputs across API calls. This applies both to Anthropic’s first-party inference service and to inference through third-party cloud providers.

## TTFT (time to first token)

Time to first token (TTFT) is a performance metric that measures the time it takes for a language model to generate the first token of its output after receiving a prompt. It is an important indicator of the model’s responsiveness and is particularly relevant for interactive applications, chatbots, and real-time systems where users expect quick initial feedback. A lower TTFT indicates that the model can start generating a response faster, providing a more seamless and engaging user experience. Factors that can influence TTFT include model size, hardware capabilities, network conditions, and the complexity of the prompt.

## Tokens

Tokens are the smallest individual units of a language model, and can correspond to words, subwords, characters, or even bytes (in the case of Unicode). For Claude, the number of characters a token represents depends on the model and the language. Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview use a newer tokenizer that produces approximately 30 percent more tokens for the same text than earlier models, on which a token represents approximately 3.5 English characters. To get exact counts, use token counting with the model you plan to use. Tokens are typically hidden when interacting with language models at the “text” level but become relevant when examining the exact inputs and outputs of a language model. When Claude is provided with text to evaluate, the text (consisting of a series of characters) is encoded into a series of tokens for the model to process. Larger tokens improve data efficiency during inference and pretraining (and are used when possible), whereas smaller tokens allow a model to handle uncommon or never-before-seen words. The choice of tokenization method can impact the model’s performance, vocabulary size, and ability to handle out-of-vocabulary words.

Anthropic.content:
# Customer support agent

## Prerequisites

To follow this guide, you need:

- A Claude API key (set as theANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable)
- Python 3.10 or later

Install the required packages:
pip install anthropic streamlit python-dotenv

## Before building with Claude

### Decide whether to use Claude for support chat

Here are some key indicators that you should employ an LLM such as Claude to automate portions of your customer support process:

### High volume of repetitive queries
Claude excels at handling a large number of similar questions efficiently, freeing up human agents for more complex issues.

### Need for quick information synthesis
Claude can quickly retrieve, process, and combine information from vast knowledge bases, whereas human agents might need time to research or consult multiple sources.

### 24/7 availability requirement
Claude can provide support at all hours without fatigue, whereas staffing human agents for continuous coverage can be costly and challenging.

### Rapid scaling during peak periods
Claude can handle sudden increases in query volume without the need for hiring and training additional staff.

### Consistent brand voice
You can instruct Claude to consistently represent your brand’s tone and values, whereas human agents might vary in their communication styles.

Some considerations for choosing Claude over other LLMs:

- You prioritize natural, nuanced conversation: Claude’s sophisticated language understanding allows for more natural, context-aware conversations that feel more human-like than chats with other LLMs.
- You often receive complex and open-ended queries: Claude can handle a wide range of topics and inquiries without generating scripted responses or requiring extensive programming of permutations of user utterances.
- You need scalable multilingual support: Claude’s multilingual capabilities allow it to engage in conversations in over 200 languages without the need for separate chatbots or extensive translation processes for each supported language.

### Define your ideal chat interaction

Outline an ideal customer interaction to define how and when you expect the customer to interact with Claude. This outline will help to determine the technical requirements of your solution.

Here is an example chat interaction for car insurance customer support:

Customer: Initiates support chat experience

- Claude: Warmly greets customer and initiates conversation

Customer: Asks about insurance for their new electric car

- Claude: Provides relevant information about electric vehicle coverage

Customer: Asks questions related to unique needs for electric vehicle insurance

- Claude: Responds with accurate and informative answers and provides links to the sources

Customer: Asks off-topic questions unrelated to insurance or cars

- Claude: Clarifies it does not discuss unrelated topics and steers the user back to car insurance

Customer: Expresses interest in an insurance quote

- Claude: Asks a set of questions to determine the appropriate quote, adapting to their responses
- Claude: Sends a request to use the quote generation API tool along with necessary information collected from the user
- Claude: Receives the response information from the API tool use, synthesizes the information into a natural response, and presents the provided quote to the user

Customer: Asks follow-up questions

- Claude: Answers follow-up questions as needed
- Claude: Guides the customer to the next steps in the insurance process and closes out the conversation

In the real example that you write for your own use case, you might find it useful to write the actual words in this interaction so that you can also get a sense of the ideal tone, response length, and level of detail you want Claude to have.

### Break the interaction into unique tasks

Customer support chat is a collection of multiple different tasks, from question answering to information retrieval to taking action on requests, wrapped up in a single customer interaction. Before you start building, break down your ideal customer interaction into every task you want Claude to be able to perform. This ensures you can prompt and evaluate Claude for every task, and gives you a good sense of the range of interactions you need to account for when writing test cases.

Customers sometimes find it helpful to visualize this as an interaction flowchart of possible conversation inflection points depending on user requests.

Here are the key tasks associated with the example insurance interaction:

Greeting and general guidance

- Warmly greet the customer and initiate conversation
- Provide general information about the company and interaction

Product information

Provide information about electric vehicle coverage This will require that Claude have the necessary information in its context, and might imply that a

is necessary.

Answer questions related to unique electric vehicle insurance needs

Answer follow-up questions about the quote or insurance details

Offer links to sources when appropriate

Conversation management

- Stay on topic (car insurance)
- Redirect off-topic questions back to relevant subjects

Quote generation

- Ask appropriate questions to determine quote eligibility
- Adapt questions based on customer responses
- Submit collected information to quote generation API
- Present the provided quote to the customer

### Establish success criteria

Work with your support team to define success criteria and write detailed evaluations with measurable benchmarks and goals.

Here are criteria and benchmarks that can be used to evaluate how successfully Claude performs the defined tasks:

### Query comprehension accuracy
This metric evaluates how accurately Claude interprets customer inquiries across various topics. Measure this by reviewing a sample of conversations and assessing whether Claude has the correct interpretation of customer intent, critical next steps, what successful resolution looks like, and more. Aim for a comprehension accuracy of 95 percent or higher.

### Response relevance
This assesses how well Claude’s response addresses the customer’s specific question or issue. Evaluate a set of conversations and rate the relevance of each response (using LLM-based grading for scale). Target a relevance score of 90 percent or above.

### Response accuracy
Assess the correctness of general company and product information provided to the user, based on the information provided to Claude in context. Target 100 percent accuracy in this introductory information.

### Citation provision relevance
Track the frequency and relevance of links or sources offered. Target providing relevant sources in 80 percent of interactions where additional information could be beneficial.

### Topic adherence
Measure how well Claude stays on topic, such as the topic of car insurance in the example implementation. Aim for 95 percent of responses to be directly related to car insurance or the customer’s specific query.

### Content generation effectiveness
Measure how successful Claude is at determining when to generate informational content and how relevant that content is. For example, in this implementation, you would be determining how well Claude identifies when to generate a quote and how accurate that quote is. Target 100 percent accuracy, as this is vital information for a successful customer interaction.

### Escalation efficiency
This measures Claude’s ability to recognize when a query needs human intervention and escalate appropriately. Track the percentage of correctly escalated conversations versus those that should have been escalated but weren’t. Aim for an escalation accuracy of 95 percent or higher.

Here are criteria and benchmarks that can be used to evaluate the business impact of employing Claude for support:

### Sentiment maintenance
This assesses Claude’s ability to maintain or improve customer sentiment throughout the conversation. Use sentiment analysis tools to measure sentiment at the beginning and end of each conversation. Aim for maintained or improved sentiment in 90 percent of interactions.

### Deflection rate
The percentage of customer inquiries successfully handled by the chatbot without human intervention. Typically aim for a 70–80 percent deflection rate, depending on the complexity of inquiries.

### Customer satisfaction score
A measure of how satisfied customers are with their chatbot interaction. Usually done through post-interaction surveys. Aim for a CSAT score of 4 out of 5 or higher.

### Average handle time
The average time it takes for the chatbot to resolve an inquiry. This varies widely based on the complexity of issues, but generally, aim for a lower AHT compared to human agents.

## How to implement Claude as a customer service agent

### Choose the right Claude model

The choice of model depends on the trade-offs among cost, accuracy, and response time.

For customer support chat, Claude Opus 5.5 is well suited to balance intelligence, latency, and cost, including the most complex support scenarios that require deep reasoning across long, multistep conversations. However, for instances where you have a conversation flow with multiple prompts including RAG, tool use, or long-context prompts, Claude Haiku 5.5 might be more suitable to optimize for latency. Effort is its main control for speed:low is the fastest level, suited to chat and short tool tasks.

### Build a strong prompt

Using Claude for customer support requires Claude having enough direction and context to respond appropriately, while having enough flexibility to handle a wide range of customer inquiries.

Start by writing the elements of a strong prompt, beginning with a system prompt. Create a file calledconfig.py and add each of the following blocks to it:
IDENTITY = """You are Eva, a friendly and knowledgeable AI assistant for Acme Insurance
Company. Your role is to warmly welcome customers and provide information on
Acme's

OpenAI.title: ChatGPT — Competitive Research
OpenAI.description: ChatGPT is OpenAI's flagship consumer AI assistant, serving 900 million weekly active users as of February 2026. It began as a purely reactive chat interface and has evolved to include Agent Mode (autonomous multi-step task execution)...
OpenAI.content:
# ChatGPT — Competitive Research

Last updated: 2026-05-05 Sources:

- https://chatgpt.com/pricing/ (403 — mirrored via third parties)
- https://openai.com/business/chatgpt-pricing/ (403 — mirrored via third parties)
- https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/chatgpt-plans-comparison
- https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-go/
- https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/
- https://openai.com/index/introducing-workspace-agents-in-chatgpt/
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10291617-scheduled-tasks-in-chatgpt
- https://chatgpt.com/features/agent/
- https://chatgpt.com/features/desktop/
- https://chatgpt.com/download/
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq
- https://felloai.com/chatgpt-pricing-guide-free-go-plus-pro-alternatives-october-2025/

## Product Overview

ChatGPT is OpenAI's flagship consumer AI assistant, serving 900 million weekly active users as of February 2026. It began as a purely reactive chat interface and has evolved to include Agent Mode (autonomous multi-step task execution), scheduled tasks, memory across sessions, workspace agents for teams, and the Atlas browser (macOS; Windows in beta). Available on web, iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows. The default model as of April 23, 2026 is GPT-5.5.

## Pricing

- Free tier: $0 — GPT-5.3 Instant, 10 messages every 5 hours, basic memory, limited deep research, ads shown (US). No agent mode.
- Go: $8/month — 10x more messages, unlimited GPT-5.3 Instant, file uploads, image creation, ads still shown, no GPT-5.5.
- Plus: $20/month — No ads, GPT-5.5 at high weekly limits, GPT-5.4 Thinking, Deep Research (10 runs/month), Sora, Codex, Agent Mode. First tier with full agent capabilities.
- Pro: $200/month — Unlimited o1/GPT-5.5 Pro access, o1 Pro mode, 5x Plus usage. (A $100/month middle tier launched April 9, 2026 offering GPT-5.5 Pro and 5x Plus usage at half the old Pro price.)
- Business: $25/user/month — Workspace agents, Slack/Google Drive/SharePoint/GitHub integrations, shared workspace, team GPTs, no data training, SOC 2 Type II.
- Enterprise: Custom pricing — All Business features + extended context (128K+), SCIM, custom data residency, 24/7 priority support, ISO 27001 certified. Source: https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/chatgpt-plans-comparison, https://felloai.com/chatgpt-pricing-guide-free-go-plus-pro-alternatives-october-2025/

## Key Capabilities

### Acts before you ask (proactive)

Partial — ChatGPT Tasks (launched January 2025, expanded 2026) allows users to set scheduled reminders and recurring tasks. ChatGPT proactively sends push notifications or emails when a scheduled task executes. Workspace Agents (Business/Enterprise, launched April 22, 2026) can run on a schedule and pick up Slack requests as they arrive. However, ChatGPT does not independently monitor your inbox or calendar and initiate contact — the user must set up the trigger. It is scheduled-reactive, not fully proactive. Source: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10291617-scheduled-tasks-in-chatgpt, https://openai.com/index/introducing-workspace-agents-in-chatgpt/

### Multi-step workflows

Yes (Plus and above) — ChatGPT Agents can reason, research, and take actions across tools in multi-step sequences using its own computer. Workspace Agents (Business/Enterprise) can run complex automations on a schedule or triggered by Slack messages. Scheduled tasks support daily/weekly/monthly recurrence, If/Then logic in plain English, and dynamic content generation (e.g. fetch stock prices at a scheduled time rather than just send a reminder). Source: https://chatgpt.com/features/agent/, https://openai.com/index/introducing-workspace-agents-in-chatgpt/

### Cross-tool memory

Yes — three-layer memory architecture: (1) Saved Memories (user facts and preferences persisted across all conversations), (2) Chat history referencing (retrieval of relevant past conversations), (3) Active session context window. Free users get lightweight continuity. Pro users get unlimited memory and maximum context. Users can turn off memory or use Temporary Chat mode. Memory uses RAG under the hood. Browser Memory (Atlas, Windows beta) also retains browsing context across sessions. Source: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq, https://www.datastudios.org/post/chatgpt-atlas-for-windows-release-date-features-agent-mode-and-browser-memory-explained

### Integrations

Count: Core integrations in Business/Enterprise: Slack, Google Drive, SharePoint, GitHub, and more. Major integrations (Business/Enterprise): Slack, Google Drive, SharePoint, GitHub; SAML/SSO; SCIM provisioning. Custom MCP / marketplace: No native MCP marketplace as a user-facing feature. GPT Builder allows custom GPT creation with actions (API integrations) on Plus and above. Workspace agents in Business can be deployed in Slack. Source: https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/chatgpt-plans-comparison

### Cross-channel chat

Web: yes Mobile (iOS): yes (official app) Mobile (Android): yes (official app) Desktop (Mac): yes (official desktop app; voice mode removed from macOS app January 15, 2026 — accessible via web and other platforms) Desktop (Windows): yes (official desktop app with full voice) Desktop (Linux): no official app (third-party wrappers exist) WhatsApp: no — not found on official sources as of 2026-05-05 Slack: yes (Workspace Agents deploy in Slack — Business/Enterprise only) Telegram: no — not found on official sources as of 2026-05-05 Discord: no — not found on official sources as of 2026-05-05 Source: https://chatgpt.com/download/, https://chatgpt.com/features/desktop/

### Unified view

No — ChatGPT does not offer a unified view combining tasks, email, calendar, and goals. The Schedules page (chatgpt.com/schedules) shows active scheduled tasks but this is not a full productivity dashboard. Chat-centric interface only. Source: https://chatgpt.com/schedules — absence of unified view noted as of 2026-05-05

### Smart todos that execute

Yes (Plus and above via Agent Mode) — ChatGPT Agent can browse the web, write and run code, manage files, interact with external services, and complete multi-step research-and-execute tasks autonomously. Users can assign complex tasks (e.g. "research competitors and draft a report") and the agent works through them step by step. Source: https://chatgpt.com/features/agent/

### Approval flow for agent actions

Yes (via SDK / Agents API) — When a tool invocation is about to execute a consequential action, the OpenAI Agents SDK evaluates approval rules. If approval is required, the run pauses and returns a RunToolApprovalItem in the interruptions array, waiting for explicit human approval, rejection, or redirect. In practice within the consumer ChatGPT interface, the agent confirms with the user before taking high-risk or irreversible actions, but the product UX for approval is less formalized than GAIA's dedicated approval flow. Source: https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/human-in-the-loop/

### Cloud vs local

Cloud-only. All processing happens on OpenAI's infrastructure. No self-hosting option. Source: https://chatgpt.com/pricing/ — no self-hosting option found as of 2026-05-05

### Open source + self-hostable

No — ChatGPT itself is closed source and cloud-only. OpenAI publishes some open-source tooling (Agents SDK, Whisper, etc.) but ChatGPT the product is not open source or self-hostable. Source: https://chatgpt.com/ — no open-source product page found as of 2026-05-05

## Where it genuinely beats GAIA

- Brand recognition and user base: 900 million weekly active users, the most widely used AI assistant on the planet. Network effects, brand trust, and ubiquity that no competitor has matched.
- Model capability: GPT-5.5 with o1 Pro mode, Deep Research (10 runs/month on Plus), and Codex give it state-of-the-art performance on complex reasoning, coding, and research tasks.
- Business/team collaboration: Workspace Agents with Slack deployment, shared GPT libraries, team workspaces, and enterprise security (SOC 2, ISO 27001, SCIM) make it the strongest option for large-team rollouts. Source: https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/chatgpt-plans-comparison, https://openai.com/index/introducing-workspace-agents-in-chatgpt/

## Summary for comparison grid

- 6 pricing tiers from $0 (Free) to custom (Enterprise); Plus at $20/month includes Agent Mode
- Available on web, iOS, Android, macOS, Windows (no Linux desktop, no WhatsApp/Telegram/Discord)
- Scheduled tasks and Workspace Agents enable proactive execution, but user must set up the trigger
- Three-layer cross-session memory included across all tiers (lightweight on free)
- Closed source, cloud-only; no self-hosting; integrations limited to Business/Enterprise tier

OpenAI.content:
# Do you know what GPT is?

GPT is a large language model developed by OpenAI with major financial backing from Microsoft, and is currently leading the market in terms of technology and capability.

AI technologies have been being developed at companies like Amazon, Google and Microsoft for some time. The first large language model, GPT-1, was released by OpenAI in 2018. It wasn't until the release of ChatGPT, which is powered by GPT, that the technology became widely known.

### Isn't it called ChatGPT?

Whilst sharing similar names ChatGPT and GPT are different. GPT stands for Generative Pretrained Transformer and refers to the large language model that underlies the ChatGPT frontend. This model accessed using an API.

This allows for developers to build their own applications leveraging the same capabilities of ChatGPT over the top of the GPT model. A great example of this is the SSW RulesGPT bot.

### Why is GPT cool?

<boxEmbed style="greybox" body={<> Why is GPT cool?

GPT is cool because it is a powerful artificial intelligence language model that can generate human-like text. It can be used for a variety of tasks, such as natural language processing, text generation, and question answering. It has the potential to revolutionize the way people interact with computers and make AI more accessible to the general public. </>} figurePrefix="none" figure="ChatGPT's response when asked "Why is GPT cool?"" />

### How does GPT work?

GPT models are trained on a huge amount of data (often refered to as parameters) that it can then use to predict what words should come next when given an input. For example, if the training data contains a weather report talking about beautiful clear blue skies, when you ask it what color the sky is it can call back to that data and respond blue.

GPT is trained on a huge amount of parameters.

- GPT-5: parameter count not publicly disclosed by OpenAI - the current generation and a significant step up from GPT-4.
- GPT-4: 1.76 trillion parameters.
- GPT-3: 175 billion parameters.
- GPT-2: 1.5 billion parameters.
- GPT-1: 117 million parameters.

### Strengths

- The model can respond to queries using natural language.
- The model can handle grammatical and spelling errors.
- Responses can come from the model very quickly - no need to access a database to retrieve data.

### Limitations

- The model is only as good as it's training data and has no knowledge of anything outside of this data.

- 重點一：OpenAI將ChatGPT dot擴大測試給部分Plus用戶。
- 重點二：dot主打全天候常駐，可跨App推進長期任務。
- 重點三：目前也同步開放Business Standard並保留額度限制。

OpenAI 在ChatGPT中推出dot ，為全天候常駐型AI智慧體（AI Agent，AI代理人 ），先前僅針對ChatGPT Pro 、Business Premium 與Enterprise用戶推出，如今OpenAI開始讓少部分ChatGPT Plus 訂閱用戶測試ChatGPT dot。

據9to5mac報導，OpenAI在今年9月公布ChatGPT dot，定位為一款全天候、主動型AI助理（AI代理人 ），可以持續處理長期任務、跨多個已連結APP工作，即使使用者沒有持續與它互動，也能自行推進專案進度。

## 支援從iOS通知直接回覆

最初，dot僅開放給Pro、Business Premium與Enterprise方案使用。OpenAI當時也說明，對Pro與Business Premium用戶來說，與ChatGPT dot的對話不會計入一般ChatGPT使用額度，不過較複雜的任務仍會受到另外的使用限制，若用戶把工作交給ChatGPT Work或Codex執行，則會分別計入這些產品本身的使用額度。

OpenAI後續也擴大ChatGPT dot所使用的模型陣容，本月稍早除了GPT-6 Astra之外，也加入GPT-6.1 Terra，還加入多項新功能 ，包含iOS小工具與捷徑整合，以及可透過iMessage與Android上的RCS與dot溝通；目前這項功能仍在美國針對Pro訂閱用戶進行Beta測試。此外，Dots也支援直接從iOS通知中回覆，並新加入自訂指令功能，讓用戶可自訂dot應該如何行動與回應。

## 目前針對少部人進行測試

負責Codex與ChatGPT工程業務的OpenAI主管Thibault Tibo Sottiaux今日宣布，公司將開始把dot的使用資格擴大到ChatGPT Plus訂閱用戶，不過現階段仍只會針對少部分人進行有限測試；同時也將把dot全面開放給ChatGPT Business Standard用戶。

ChatGPT Plus每月定價為270元、ChatGPT Pro每月為690元，換句話說，可以用便宜的價格來執行dot，不過目前還尚未得知ChatGPT Plus與Business Standard用戶是否能享有與高階方案相同的dot使用額度，或是否會有額外限制。

# DeepMind’s AI agents found cheaper quantum algorithms, and proved them

Teams of Gemini 4 agents cut a fusion simulation's cost nearly 12-fold, with every result mathematically proved.

Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI used teams of Gemini 4 agents to find more efficient quantum algorithms for fusion, chemistry and drug-design problems. Each result was proved correct in the Lean theorem prover, because the circuits are too large to test on today’s computers.

Google DeepMind says teams of AI agents have found faster quantum algorithms for problems in fusion energy, chemistry and drug design. The agents, running on Gemini 4, proved each result correct with Lean, a tool that checks mathematical proofs, the lab said on Monday.

The proofs matter because the circuits are too big to test. They need thousands of qubits, far beyond what classical computers can simulate or today’s quantum chips can run.

The biggest gain came in a fusion problem. The agents cut the cost of a quantum calculation for laser-driven fusion fuel by 11.8 times, and its memory from 5,650 to 4,338 error-corrected qubits, DeepMind says.

They also made a simulation of a light-sensitive molecule about eight times cheaper. For Cytochrome P450, an enzyme that breaks down most medicines, the cost fell 2.5 times. A widely used maths routine became more than 290 times cheaper.

Separate agent teams worked on each problem and shared verified ideas in a common notebook. Every four hours, they met in a virtual conference to debate and compare approaches. The work, with Google Quantum AI, used Google’s most powerful model, Gemini 4 Carbon.

An outside checker re-ran every proof so agents could not game the tests, according to the paper. That risk is real: in a DeepMind experiment in September, 14% of agents cheated on Lean maths problems.

DeepMind cautions that the simulations would still need far more resources than the first error-corrected quantum computers will offer. It has open-sourced its Lean library and results, building on its 2024 work to trim quantum circuits with AlphaTensor-Quantum. Earlier this month, its agents also proved Signal’s encryption code correct, and Google Quantum AI tested a key quantum effect on up to 105 qubits.

# 谷歌 DeepMind 发布世界模型 Genie 4：实时交互世界、原生音频，与 Gemini 深度整合

举报

yd_224132983 发表于 2026/11/23 10:19:13 2026/11/23

3 0 0

【摘要】 谷歌 DeepMind 10 月 27 日发布新一代世界模型 Genie 4：实时交互、自然语言改写世界、原生音频，并与 Gemini 深度结合，目前以研究预览向受信任测试者开放。

2026 年 10 月 27 日，谷歌 DeepMind 发布新一代世界模型 Genie 4，这是继 2025 年 8 月 Genie 3 之后，该系列的又一次重要更新。与只能生成视频片段的生成模型不同，Genie 4 的目标是“可走进去的世界”：用户用文字或图片给出提示，就能得到一个可以实时探索、实时改动的交互式三维世界。

一、实时改写世界：自然语言即时修改模拟

Genie 4 最直观的变化，是模拟过程可以边玩边改。用户在模拟进行中使用自然语言，就能实时调整世界中的元素，比如改变天气、增减物体、切换场景氛围，修改会立即反映在正在运行的模拟里，不需要重新生成。DeepMind 把这种能力称为“实时塑造世界模拟”。

二、真实感再进一步：物理与人物动作

Genie 4 在实时交互模拟的真实感上设立了新标准。模型对物理规律的模拟更扎实，人物角色的动作也更自然：角色会自然地移动，并对环境做出反应。DeepMind 表示，这是 Genie 4 相比前代最显著的进步之一，人物模拟是其中的重点。

三、第一次原生音频：环境音与交互对话

Genie 4 是 DeepMind 首个原生生成音频的实时世界模型。每个生成的世界都自带环境音效；更进一步的是，模型还引入了交互式对话能力，世界中的角色可以根据情境与用户对话，语音会随场景变化而调整。画面、声音与交互第一次在同一个实时模型里打通。

四、与 Gemini 结合：复杂事件模拟与机器人

Genie 4 融合了 Gemini 家族的能力。在复杂事件模拟中，Gemini 3.8 Flash 作为循环中的引导智能体，在 Genie 4 生成画面的同时负责推理与规划，让多步骤的事件链条按逻辑推进。DeepMind 还在尝试把 Gemini 4 Argon 与 Genie 4 结合，用于机器人研究，例如模拟 Apptronik 的 Apollo 人形机器人参与游戏任务。DeepMind 认为，理解并模拟世界是通向通用人工智能（AGI）的关键一环，Genie 4 正是在这条路上的进展。

五、开放节奏与使用边界

Genie 4 目前以研究预览的形式向受信任的测试者开放，官方同时开放了候补名单，并表示即将面向 Google AI Ultra 用户推出。受信任测试者的反馈集中在几个方向：创意工作者把它当作预可视化的快速“草稿模式”；摄影记者尝试用一张二维档案照片生成可进入的沉浸式历史场景；游戏开发者用它从初步想法快速做出可交互的体验概念；企业合作伙伴则在评估它作为仿真工具的价值。

需要提醒的是，Genie 4 仍是早期的实验性模型。DeepMind 明确指出，它能在短会话中保持环境连贯，但随着会话变长，视觉细节与物体恒常性会有所下降。生成的所有视频与音频都会带有 SynthID 水印，以标明 AI 生成内容。

六、对开发者意味着什么

对开发者来说，Genie 4 的意义不只是“更好看的生成视频”，而是世界模型正在成为一种新的开发素材：交互式仿真、机器人训练环境、游戏原型、沉浸式内容，都可能从“先建模再渲染”变成“先描述再进入”。当然，现阶段它更适合探索与原型验证，真正落地到生产流程，还要等模型在长会话稳定性、细节一致性上继续成熟。

本文信息来源为 Google DeepMind 官方博客（2026 年 10 月 27 日发布的《Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation》）及公开报道，关键事实均以公开信息为准。

Google.content:
# Google integrations

Source: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/javascript/integrations/providers/google

Integrate with Google using LangChain JavaScript.

LangChain provides integrations with Google AI Studio and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform through the@langchain/google package.

[!NOTE]

Looking for the older
@langchain/google-genai or @langchain/google-vertexai packages? They are maintained under long-term support but are no longer recommended for new projects.

## Chat models

TheChatGoogle class is the recommended way to access Gemini models (such as gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-4-hydrogen, and gemini-3.1-pro-preview) and open models like Gemma. It supports both Google AI Studio and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform in a single interface

[!TIP]

See this section for general instructions on installing LangChain packages.
npm install @langchain/google @langchain/core
yarn add @langchain/google @langchain/core
pnpm add @langchain/google @langchain/core

Configure your API key:
export GOOGLE_API_KEY=your-api-key
import { ChatGoogle } from "@langchain/google";

const model = new ChatGoogle("gemini-4-hydrogen");

const res = await model.invoke([
  ["human", "What would be a good company name for a company that makes colorful socks?"],
]);

ChatGoogle supports tool calling, structured output, multimodal inputs (images, audio, video), reasoning/thinking, image generation, text-to-speech, and Gemini-specific native tools like Google Search grounding and code execution.

[card] ChatGoogle

Full chat model documentation, including setup, invocation, streaming, structured output, and more.

[card] Gemini native tools

Google Search, Code Execution, URL Context, Google Maps, File Search, Computer Use, and MCP servers.

### Third-party models on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

Anthropic Claude models are also available through the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform platform. See using Claude on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform for more information about enabling access to the models and the model names to use.

### Postgres vector store (Cloud SQL)

The PostgresVectorStore module from the@langchain/google-cloud-sql-pg package provides a way to use CloudSQL for PostgreSQL to store
vector embeddings.
npm install @langchain/google-cloud-sql-pg @langchain/core

## Decision models

[card] GoogleClassifier

Typed answers and probabilities from the Gemini Decisions API for routing, classification, and review.

## Legacy packages

The following packages are maintained under long-term support for existing users. New projects should use@langchain/google instead.

### @langchain/google-genai

The@langchain/google-genai package provides ChatGoogleGenerativeAI and GoogleGenerativeAIEmbeddings for accessing Gemini models through Google AI Studio. This package is built on a deprecated Google SDK and will not receive new features.
npm install @langchain/google-genai @langchain/core

### @langchain/google-vertexai

The@langchain/google-vertexai package provides ChatVertexAI, VertexAIEmbeddings, and VertexAI for Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform on Node.js. It depends on @langchain/google-gauth for authentication. This package is superseded by the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform support built into @langchain/google for chat.
npm install @langchain/google-vertexai @langchain/core

### @langchain/google-vertexai-web

The@langchain/google-vertexai-web package provides the same Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform chat, embedding, and LLM classes for browser and Edge runtimes. Install this package (not @langchain/google-vertexai) when running in web environments. It depends on @langchain/google-webauth.
npm install @langchain/google-vertexai-web @langchain/core

See the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform chat page forGOOGLE_WEB_CREDENTIALS and web import paths.

### @langchain/google-webauth

The@langchain/google-webauth package provides browser and Edge authentication for legacy Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform integrations. It is installed automatically with @langchain/google-vertexai-web—do not install it alongside @langchain/google-gauth.

Set service account JSON inGOOGLE_WEB_CREDENTIALS (or the deprecated GOOGLE_VERTEX_AI_WEB_CREDENTIALS). You can also pass apiKey or authOptions to the model constructor, or set the API_KEY environment variable.

### @langchain/google-gauth

The@langchain/google-gauth package provides Node.js authentication for legacy Google integrations built on @langchain/google-common. It is installed automatically when you add @langchain/google-vertexai—you typically do not install or import @langchain/google-gauth directly.

On Node.js, credentials are resolved in this order:

- apiKey passed to the model constructor
- authOptions passed to the model constructor
- TheAPI_KEY environment variable
- Service account JSON at the path inGOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
- Application Default Credentials (for example aftergcloud auth application-default login, or on Google Cloud)

Do not use@langchain/google-gauth and @langchain/google-webauth in the same project.

The unified@langchain/google package uses google-auth-library directly and does not require @langchain/google-gauth or @langchain/google-webauth.

### @langchain/google-cloud-sql-pg

The@langchain/google-cloud-sql-pg package provides PostgresVectorStore and PostgresLoader for Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL. It is separate from the Gemini chat packages above.

### @langchain/google-common

The@langchain/google-common package provides shared Gemini client abstractions for legacy integrations such as @langchain/google-vertexai. It does not include authorization code and is not a stand-alone package—do not install or import it directly.

[!TIP]

To migrate from
@langchain/google-genai or @langchain/google-vertexai to @langchain/google, see the ChatGoogle page for setup instructions. The ChatGoogle class provides equivalent functionality with unified access to both Google AI Studio and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.
Connect these docs to your agent of choice via MCP for real-time answers.

Google.content:
Gemini 4 Neon 推出；在相對強弱指數猜測之際，Gemini 5 開發工作正進行中

關鍵要點

Google DeepMind 於 2026 年 11 月 18 日在 Gemini app、Google AI Studio 和 Google Antigravity 發布 Gemini 4 Neon，提供 100 萬代幣的上下文視窗和四種思考層級。

根據官方基準測試結果，Gemini 4 Neon 在 19 項受評測的基準測試中，有 17 項的表現優於 Claude Opus 5.5 和 GPT-6.2 Sol；在 CursorBench 4.1 上的表現則達 65.4%。

DeepMind 研究員 Minkai Xu 表示，遞迴式自我改進可能加速 Gemini 5 的開發，不過 Google 尚未公布 Gemini 5 的官方規格或發布日期。

Google DeepMind 於 2026 年 11 月 18 日發布 Gemini 4 Neon，完成以元素週期表為主題、快速推出前沿模型的計畫。這波發布引發了外界對遞迴自我改進及 Gemini 5 加速開發的猜測。此前推出的 Gemini 4 Argon、Carbon 和 Hydrogen，彼此間隔僅數週，而非主要模型升級之間傳統的一年週期。業界觀察人士注意到，DeepMind 研究人員 Vedant Misra 和 Minkai Xu 在社群媒體上發布了隱晦的暗示，似乎表明內部回饋迴圈可能正加快每一代模型的開發。

Gemini 4 Neon 規格與效能

Gemini 4 Neon 以 Gemini 4 Carbon 為基礎，並部署於 Gemini 應用程式、Google AI Studio 和 Google Antigravity，具備 100 萬詞元的上下文視窗，以及低、中、高和超高四種可調整的思考等級。定價為每百萬個輸入詞元 3 美元，每百萬個輸出詞元 15 美元。根據 Google DeepMind 官方的 Gemini 4 Neon Model Card，該模型在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 上獲得 61 分。

在比較基準測試中，Gemini 4 Neon 在 19 項評估基準中的 17 項勝過 Claude Opus 5.5 和 GPT-6.2 Sol。在 CursorBench 4.1 上，Neon 使用超高推理設定時達到 65.4%。在 GraphWalks 長上下文檢索測試中，該模型達到 95.2%。開發者表示，該模型在多檔案重構和 Rust 效能最佳化方面展現出精準度。早期採用者指出仍有改善空間，包括最高思考預算下的尾端延遲，以及更完善的提示快取控制；Google 工程團隊正積極徵求意見，以發布小幅更新。

週期表式發布：從 Argon 到 Neon

Google DeepMind 迅速接連推出 Gemini 4 模型，滿足不同專業用途。Gemini 4 Argon 是此系列首款推出的前沿模型。Gemini 4 Carbon 定位為深度思考專家，適用於長期工程任務、複雜的架構決策和網路安全。接著推出的 Gemini 4 Hydrogen，則能以超快速度和低成本執行大量工作流程、子代理協調作業，並整合至 Google Search。Gemini 4 Neon 於 11 月 18 日補齊產品陣容，在接近 Carbon 的智慧程度之上，兼具正式部署所需的速度與成本效益。

遞迴自我改進猜測與 Gemini 5 訊號

緊湊的發布時程引發業界對遞迴自我改進（RSI）的討論。這個概念指的是，AI 系統能力提升到足以協助設計自身後繼模型、為其生成合成訓練資料，或最佳化其程式碼與架構。Neon 發布前一晚，DeepMind 研究人員 Minkai Xu 在 X 發文表示「許多人都對 RSI 發展得如此迅速感到驚訝」，《The Rundown AI》的報導引述了這則貼文。Gemini 核心團隊成員 Vedant Misra 自 Gemini 1 至 Gemini 4 以來一直是推理能力開發的關鍵人物；在 Gemini 4 Neon 開發仍在進行之際，他已暗示後續發展。

在實際部署方面，Google 可利用 Carbon 這類高強度推理模型，生成經驗證的合成軌跡、整理出更乾淨的訓練資料集，並在 Antigravity 等環境中自動化強化學習迴圈。這個過程能讓公司將智慧蒸餾至 Neon 這類更快速、成本更低的模型，同時為下一代模型啟動預訓練與後訓練作業。

開發軌跡與產業影響

Google 尚未公布 Gemini 5 的正式發布日期或規格表。Neon 發布前兩個月所展現的發展軌跡，顯示前沿 AI 實驗室的運作方式正在轉變。以往單一大型模型發布間隔長達 12 個月，如今已縮短至數週。Gemini 4 Neon 已與 Hydrogen 一同為代理式程式碼開發和多模型協調作業樹立新標準；在後續版本推出前，開發者將面臨快速遷移正式環境流程的壓力。

關鍵事實

Gemini 4 Neon 於 2026 年 11 月 18 日推出，部署於 Gemini 應用程式、Google AI Studio 和 Google Antigravity，具備 100 萬詞元的上下文視窗及四種思考等級（低、中、高、超高）

常見問題

Gemini 4 Neon 的主要規格與定價為何？

Gemini 4 Neon 具備 100 萬詞元的上下文視窗，以及低、中、高和超高四種可調整的思考等級。定價為每百萬個輸入詞元 3 美元，每百萬個輸出詞元 15 美元。該模型以 Gemini 4 Carbon 為基礎，並自 2026 年 11 月 18 日起部署於 Gemini 應用程式、Google AI Studio 和 Google Antigravity。

绿涨红跌

涨跌幅与 K 线开盘时间

24 小时制

Gemini 4 Neon 发布；Gemini 5 开发工作正在进行，市场对相对强弱指数的猜测不断

关键要点

谷歌 DeepMind 于 2026 年 11 月 18 日在 Gemini 应用、Google AI Studio 和 Google Antigravity 发布 Gemini 4 Neon，提供 100 万词元的上下文窗口和四种思考等级。

根据官方基准测试，Gemini 4 Neon 在评估的 19 项基准测试中有 17 项表现优于 Claude Opus 5.5 和 GPT-6.2 Sol，并在 CursorBench 4.1 上达到 65.4%。

DeepMind 研究员 Minkai Xu 表示，递归自我改进或可加速 Gemini 5 的开发，不过谷歌尚未公布 Gemini 5 的官方规格或发布日期。

Google DeepMind 于 2026 年 11 月 18 日发布 Gemini 4 Neon，完成了以元素周期表为主题的前沿模型快速发布序列。这一节奏引发了外界对递归自我改进以及 Gemini 5 加速开发的猜测。此前，Gemini 4 Argon、Carbon 和 Hydrogen 已相继部署，间隔仅数周，而非重大模型升级之间传统的一年。业内人士注意到，DeepMind 研究员 Vedant Misra 和 Minkai Xu 在社交媒体上发布了含义隐晦的暗示，似乎表明内部反馈循环可能正在加速每一代模型的开发。

Gemini 4 Neon 的规格与性能

Gemini 4 Neon 基于 Gemini 4 Carbon 改进而来，并部署于 Gemini 应用、Google AI Studio 和 Google Antigravity，具备 100 万 token 的上下文窗口和四种可调思考等级：low、medium、high 和 xhigh。其定价为每 100 万个输入 token 3 美元，每 100 万个输出 token 15 美元。根据 Google DeepMind 官方 Gemini 4 Neon Model Card，该模型在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 上得分为 61。

在对比基准测试中，Gemini 4 Neon 在评估的 19 项基准中有 17 项优于 Claude Opus 5.5 和 GPT-6.2 Sol。在 CursorBench 4.1 上，Neon 在 xhigh 推理设置下取得了 65.4% 的成绩。在 GraphWalks 长上下文检索测试中，该模型达到了 95.2%。开发者表示，该模型在多文件重构和 Rust 性能优化方面展现出较高精度。早期用户指出仍有改进空间，包括思考预算达到最大值时的尾延迟，以及更精细的提示缓存控制；Google 工程团队正积极征求反馈，以进行小版本更新。

周期表式发布序列：从 Argon 到 Neon

Google DeepMind 针对不同专业用途接连快速部署 Gemini 4 系列模型。Gemini 4 Argon 是该系列最初发布的前沿模型。Gemini 4 Carbon 被定位为深度思考专家，适用于长周期工程任务、复杂架构决策和网络安全。随后推出的 Gemini 4 Hydrogen 执行速度极快、成本低，适用于高吞吐量工作流、子智能体编排以及集成至 Google 搜索。Gemini 4 Neon 于 11 月 18 日补齐了这一阵容，在接近 Carbon 的智能水平与生产部署所需的速度和价格优势之间实现了平衡。

递归自我改进猜测与 Gemini 5 信号

紧凑的发布日程引发了业内对递归自我改进（RSI）的讨论。这个概念指的是，AI 系统的能力足以协助设计后继系统、为其生成合成训练数据，或优化其代码和架构。Neon 发布前一晚，DeepMind 研究员 Minkai Xu 在 X 上发帖称，“许多人都对 RSI 发展得如此之快感到惊讶”，The Rundown AI 的报道提到了这条帖子。核心 Gemini 团队成员 Vedant Misra 一直参与从 Gemini 1 到 Gemini 4 的推理能力关键研发工作；在 Gemini 4 Neon 仍在开发期间，他已暗示了后续发展。

在实际部署中，Google 可以利用 Carbon 这类强推理模型生成经过验证的合成轨迹、筛选更优质的训练数据集，并在 Antigravity 等环境中自动化强化学习循环。这样一来，公司就能将智能提炼到 Neon 这类更快速、成本更低的模型中，同时为下一代模型启动预训练和后训练流程。

开发轨迹与行业影响

Google 尚未公布 Gemini 5 的官方发布日期或规格表。Neon 发布前两个月形成的开发轨迹，预示着前沿 AI 实验室的运作方式正在发生转变。过去单个大型模型发布之间传统的 12 个月间隔，如今已缩短至数周。Gemini 4 Neon 已与 Hydrogen 一同在智能体编程和多模型编排方面树立了新的节奏，开发者因此必须在后续版本到来前快速完成生产流水线迁移。

Llama 3.3 70B is a large language model by Meta, available on the Venice API asllama-3.3-70b. This model is private and no prompt data is stored in any capacity.

Llama 3.3 70B is Meta's instruction-tuned 70-billion-parameter Llama model, which Meta reports performs close to its much larger Llama 3.1 405B on many tasks. It supports text input and output with a 128K-token context window, for chat, writing and code.

Meta.title: 使用 Llama Stack 和 Milvus 构建 RAG
Meta.description: Llama Stack是一种面向服务、以 API 为先的架构，用于构建生产级 AI 应用程序。它提供了一个通用技术栈，使开发者能够随时随地进行开发 ... 并利用真正独立于提供商的、已准备就绪的生产级构建模块。Llama Stack 专注于 Meta 的 Llama 模型、可组合性、生产就绪性以及合作伙伴生态系统。
Meta.content:
# 使用 Llama Stack 和 Milvus 构建 RAG

Llama Stack是一种面向服务、以 API 为先的架构，用于构建生产级 AI 应用程序。它提供了一个通用技术栈，使开发者能够随时随地进行开发、部署，并利用真正独立于提供商的、已准备就绪的生产级构建模块。Llama Stack 专注于 Meta 的 Llama 模型、可组合性、生产就绪性以及合作伙伴生态系统。

在本教程中，我们将介绍如何构建一个配置了 Milvus 的 Llama Stack 服务器，使您能够导入私有数据作为知识库。随后，我们将对该服务器进行查询，从而创建一个完整的 RAG 应用程序。

## 准备环境

启动 Llama Stack 服务器有多种方式，例如作为库使用、构建发行版等。对于 Llama Stack 中的每个组件，也可以选择不同的提供商。因此，启动 Llama Stack 服务器的方式多种多样。

本教程以以下配置为例来启动该服务。如果您希望采用其他方式启动，请参阅《启动 Llama Stack 服务器》。

- 我们使用 Conda 构建包含 Milvus 配置的自定义发行版。
- 我们使用Together AI作为 LLM 提供商。
- 我们使用默认的all-MiniLM-L6-v2 作为嵌入模型。

本教程主要参考Llama Stack 文档中的官方安装指南。如果您在本教程中发现任何过时的内容，请优先遵循官方指南，并为我们提交一个问题。

## 启动 Llama Stack 服务器

### 准备环境

由于我们需要使用 Together AI 作为 LLM 服务，因此必须先登录其官方网站申请API 密钥，并将 API 密钥TOGETHER_API_KEY 设置为环境变量。

克隆 Llama Stack 源代码
$ git clone https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-stack.git
$ cd llama-stack

创建 conda 环境并安装依赖项
$ conda create -n stack python=3.10
$ conda activate stack

$ pip install -e .

修改llama_stack/llama_stack/templates/together/run.yaml 中的内容，将 vector_io 部分替换为相应的 Milvus 配置。例如，添加：
vector_io:
- provider_id: milvus
  provider_type: inline::milvus
  config:
    db_path: ~/.llama/distributions/together/milvus_store.db

#  - provider_id: milvus
#    provider_type: remote::milvus
#    config:
#      uri: http://localhost:19530
#      token: root:Milvus

在 Llama Stack 中，Milvus 可以通过两种方式进行配置：本地配置（即inline::milvus ）和远程配置（即remote::milvus ）。

- 最简单的方法是本地配置，这需要设置db_path ，即用于本地存储Milvus-Lite文件的路径。
- 远程配置适用于大规模数据存储。
- 如果您拥有大量数据，可以在Docker 或 Kubernetes 上搭建一台高性能的 Milvus 服务器。在此配置中，请将服务器 URI（例如http://localhost:19530 ）作为您的uri 。默认的token 为root:Milvus 。

- 如果您希望使用Zilliz Cloud（Milvus 的全托管云服务），请调整uri 和token ，它们分别对应 Zilliz Cloud中的公共端点和 API 密钥。

- 如果您希望使用Zilliz Cloud（Milvus 的全托管云服务），请调整

### 从模板构建发行版

运行以下命令构建发行版：
$ llama stack build --template together --image-type conda

系统将在~/.llama/distributions/together/together-run.yaml 生成一个文件。随后，运行以下命令启动服务器：
$ llama stack run --image-type conda ~/.llama/distributions/together/together-run.yaml

如果一切顺利，您应该会看到 Llama Stack 服务器已在端口 8321 上成功运行。

## 从客户端执行 RAG

启动服务器后，您可以编写客户端代码来访问它。以下是一个示例代码：
import uuid
from llama_stack_client.types import Document
from llama_stack_client.lib.agents.agent import Agent
from llama_stack_client.types.agent_create_params import AgentConfig

# See https://www.together.ai/models for all available models
INFERENCE_MODEL = "meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo"
LLAMA_STACK_PORT = 8321

def create_http_client():
    from llama_stack_client import LlamaStackClient

    return LlamaStackClient(
        base_url=f"http://localhost:{LLAMA_STACK_PORT}"  # Your Llama Stack Server URL
    )

client = create_http_client()

# Documents to be used for RAG
urls = ["chat.rst", "llama3.rst", "memory_optimizations.rst", "lora_finetune.rst"]
documents = [
    Document(
        document_id=f"num-{i}",
        content=f"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/torchtune/main/docs/source/tutorials/{url}",
        mime_type="text/plain",
        metadata={},
    )
    for i, url in enumerate(urls)
]

# Register a vector database
vector_db_id = f"test-vector-db-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
client.vector_dbs.register(
    vector_db_id=vector_db_id,
    embedding_model="all-MiniLM-L6-v2",
    embedding_dimension=384,
    provider_id="milvus",
)

print("inserting...")
# Insert the documents into the vector database
client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.insert(
    documents=documents, vector_db_id=vector_db_id, chunk_size_in_tokens=1024,
)

agent_config = AgentConfig(
    model=INFERENCE_MODEL,
    # Define instructions for the agent ( aka system prompt)
    instructions="You are a helpful assistant",
    enable_session_persistence=False,
    # Define tools available to the agent
    toolgroups=[{"name": "builtin::rag", "args": {"vector_db_ids": [vector_db_id]}}],
)

rag_agent = Agent(client, agent_config)
session_id = rag_agent.create_session("test-session")
print("finish init agent...")
user_prompt = (
    "What are the top 5 topics that were explained? Only list succinct bullet points."
)

# Get the final answer from the agent
response = rag_agent.create_turn(
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user_prompt}],
    session_id=session_id,
    stream=False,
)
print(f"Response: ")
print(response.output_message.content)

运行此代码以执行 RAG 查询。 如果一切正常，输出应如下所示：
inserting...
finish init agent...
Response:
* Fine-Tuning Llama3 with Chat Data
* Evaluating fine-tuned Llama3-8B models with EleutherAI's Eval Harness
* Generating text with our fine-tuned Llama3 model
* Faster generation via quantization
* Fine-tuning on a custom chat dataset

Meta.content:
# Build RAG with Llama Stack with Milvus

Llama Stack is a service-oriented, API-first approach for building production AI applications. It provides a universal stack that allows developers to develop anywhere, deploy everywhere, and leverage production-ready building blocks with true provider independence. The Llama Stack focuses on Meta's Llama models, composability, production-readiness, and a partnering ecosystem.

In this tutorial, we will introduce how to build a Llama Stack Server configured with Milvus, enabling you to import your private data to serve as your knowledge base. We will then perform queries on the server, creating a complete RAG application.

## Preparing the Environment

There are many ways to start the Llama Stack server, such as as a library, building a distribution, etc. For each component in the Llama Stack, various providers can also be chosen. Therefore, there are numerous ways to launch the Llama Stack server.

This tutorial uses the following configuration as an example to start the service. If you wish to start it in another way, please refer to Starting a Llama Stack Server.

- We use Conda to build a custom distribution with Milvus configuration.
- We use Together AI as the LLM provider.
- We use the defaultall-MiniLM-L6-v2 as the embedding model.

This tutorial mainly refers to the official installation guide of the Llama Stack documentation. If you find any outdated parts in this tutorial, you can prioritize following the official guide and create an issue for us.

## Start Llama Stack Server

### Prepare the Environment

Since we need to use Together AI as the LLM service, we must first log in to the official website to apply for an API key and set the API keyTOGETHER_API_KEY as an environment variable.

Clone the Llama Stack source code
$ git clone https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-stack.git
$ cd llama-stack

Create a conda environment and install dependencies
$ conda create -n stack python=3.10
$ conda activate stack

$ pip install -e .

Modify the content inllama_stack/llama_stack/template/together/run.yaml, changing the vector_io section to the relevant Milvus configuration. For example, add:
vector_io:
- provider_id: milvus
  provider_type: inline::milvus
  config:
    db_path: ~/.llama/distributions/together/milvus_store.db

#  - provider_id: milvus
#    provider_type: remote::milvus
#    config:
#      uri: http://localhost:19530
#      token: root:Milvus

In Llama Stack, Milvus can be configured in two ways: local configuration, which isinline::milvus, and remote configuration, which is remote::milvus.

The simplest method is local configuration, which requires setting
db_path, a path for locally storing Milvus-Lite files.

Remote configuration is suitable for large data storage.

- If you have a large amount of data, you can set up a performant Milvus server on Docker or Kubernetes. In this setup, please use the server URI, e.g.,http://localhost:19530, as your uri. The default token is root:Milvus.
- If you want to use Zilliz Cloud, the fully managed cloud service for Milvus, adjust theuri and token, which correspond to the Public Endpoint and API key in Zilliz Cloud.

- If you have a large amount of data, you can set up a performant Milvus server on Docker or Kubernetes. In this setup, please use the server URI, e.g.,

### Build distribution from the template

Run the following command to build the distribution:
$ llama stack build --template together --image-type conda

A file will be generated at~/.llama/distributions/together/together-run.yaml. Then, run this command to start the server:
$ llama stack run --image-type conda ~/.llama/distributions/together/together-run.yaml

If everything goes smoothly, you should see the Llama Stack server successfully running on port 8321.

## Perform RAG from client

Once you have started the server, you can write the client code to access it. Here is a sample code:
import uuid
from llama_stack_client.types import Document
from llama_stack_client.lib.agents.agent import Agent
from llama_stack_client.types.agent_create_params import AgentConfig

# See https://www.together.ai/models for all available models
INFERENCE_MODEL = "meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo"
LLAMA_STACK_PORT = 8321

def create_http_client():
    from llama_stack_client import LlamaStackClient

    return LlamaStackClient(
        base_url=f"http://localhost:{LLAMA_STACK_PORT}"  # Your Llama Stack Server URL
    )

client = create_http_client()

# Documents to be used for RAG
urls = ["chat.rst", "llama3.rst", "memory_optimizations.rst", "lora_finetune.rst"]
documents = [
    Document(
        document_id=f"num-{i}",
        content=f"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/torchtune/main/docs/source/tutorials/{url}",
        mime_type="text/plain",
        metadata={},
    )
    for i, url in enumerate(urls)
]

# Register a vector database
vector_db_id = f"test-vector-db-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
client.vector_dbs.register(
    vector_db_id=vector_db_id,
    embedding_model="all-MiniLM-L6-v2",
    embedding_dimension=384,
    provider_id="milvus",
)

print("inserting...")
# Insert the documents into the vector database
client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.insert(
    documents=documents, vector_db_id=vector_db_id, chunk_size_in_tokens=1024,
)

agent_config = AgentConfig(
    model=INFERENCE_MODEL,
    # Define instructions for the agent ( aka system prompt)
    instructions="You are a helpful assistant",
    enable_session_persistence=False,
    # Define tools available to the agent
    toolgroups=[{"name": "builtin::rag", "args": {"vector_db_ids": [vector_db_id]}}],
)

rag_agent = Agent(client, agent_config)
session_id = rag_agent.create_session("test-session")
print("finish init agent...")
user_prompt = (
    "What are the top 5 topics that were explained? Only list succinct bullet points."
)

# Get the final answer from the agent
response = rag_agent.create_turn(
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user_prompt}],
    session_id=session_id,
    stream=False,
)
print(f"Response: ")
print(response.output_message.content)

Run this code to perform the RAG query. If everything is working properly, the output should look like this:
inserting...
finish init agent...
Response:
* Fine-Tuning Llama3 with Chat Data
* Evaluating fine-tuned Llama3-8B models with EleutherAI's Eval Harness
* Generating text with our fine-tuned Llama3 model
* Faster generation via quantization
* Fine-tuning on a custom chat dataset

# 使用 Milvus 的 Llama Stack 建立 RAG

Llama Stack是一種以服務為導向、API 為先的方法，可用於建立生產型 AI 應用程式。它提供了一個通用的堆疊，讓開發人員可以隨處開發、隨處部署，並利用生產就緒的構建區塊，真正獨立於提供商。Llama Stack 著重於 Meta 的 Llama 模型、可複合性、生產就绪性以及合作生態系統。

在本教程中，我們將介紹如何使用 Milvus 建立 Llama Stack 伺服器，讓您能夠匯入私人資料作為您的知識庫。然後，我們將在伺服器上執行查詢，建立完整的 RAG 應用程式。

## 準備環境

有許多方式可以啟動 Llama Stack 伺服器，例如作為一個函式庫，建立一個發行版等等。對於 Llama Stack 中的每個元件，也可以選擇各種提供者。因此，有許多啟動 Llama Stack 伺服器的方式。

本教學使用下列配置作為啟動服務的範例。如果您希望以其他方式啟動，請參閱啟動Llama Stack 伺服器。

- 我們使用 Conda 以 Milvus 組態建立自訂的發行版。
- 我們使用Together AI作為 LLM 提供者。
- 我們使用預設的all-MiniLM-L6-v2 作為嵌入模型。

本教學主要參考Llama Stack 文件的官方安裝指南。如果您在本教學中發現任何過時的部分，您可以優先遵循官方指南，並為我們建立一個問題。

## 啟動 Llama Stack 伺服器

### 準備環境

由於我們需要使用 Together AI 作為 LLM 服務，因此必須先登入官方網站申請API key，並將 API keyTOGETHER_API_KEY 設定為環境變數。

克隆 Llama Stack 原始碼
$ git clone https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-stack.git
$ cd llama-stack

建立 conda 環境並安裝相依性
$ conda create -n stack python=3.10
$ conda activate stack

$ pip install -e .

修改llama_stack/llama_stack/template/together/run.yaml 中的內容，將 vector_io 部分改成相關的 Milvus 設定。例如，新增
vector_io:
- provider_id: milvus
  provider_type: inline::milvus
  config:
    db_path: ~/.llama/distributions/together/milvus_store.db

#  - provider_id: milvus
#    provider_type: remote::milvus
#    config:
#      uri: http://localhost:19530
#      token: root:Milvus

在 Llama Stack 中，Milvus 有兩種配置方式：本地配置，即inline::milvus ；遠端配置，即remote::milvus 。

- 最簡單的方法是本地配置，需要設定db_path ，這是本地儲存Milvus-Lite檔案的路徑。
- 遠端設定適合大量資料儲存。
- 如果您有大量的資料，您可以在Docker 或 Kubernetes 上架設效能優異的 Milvus 伺服器。在此設定中，請使用伺服器 URI，例如http://localhost:19530 ，作為您的uri 。預設的token 是root:Milvus 。

- 如果您想使用Zilliz Cloud（Milvus 的完全管理雲端服務），請調整uri 和token ，它們對應於 Zilliz Cloud 中的Public Endpoint 和 API key。

- 如果您想使用Zilliz Cloud（Milvus 的完全管理雲端服務），請調整

### 從模板建立發行版

執行下列指令建立發行版：
$ llama stack build --template together --image-type conda

將產生檔案~/.llama/distributions/together/together-run.yaml 。然後，執行此指令啟動伺服器：
$ llama stack run --image-type conda ~/.llama/distributions/together/together-run.yaml

如果一切順利，您應該會看到 Llama Stack 伺服器成功在 8321 連接埠上執行。

## 從用戶端執行 RAG

啟動伺服器後，您就可以寫用戶端程式碼來存取伺服器。以下是範例程式碼：

# DeepSeek免费限额大模型竞争迈向“价值时代”

中国工业报 王珊珊

对普通用户而言，DeepSeek的“免费午餐”或许不那么好吃了。

近日，有媒体爆出，DeepSeek对免费用户使用政策作出调整，引发行业广泛关注。网页端与APP端单次输入上限调整至约4万字，超过7天无活跃交互的长对话不再支持接续，每日对话额度另设上限。这是DeepSeek成立以来首次对免费用户进行系统性用量管理。

截至发稿，DeepSeek官方尚未发布统一的限额规则及相关说明，也未披露限制何时解除。但在外界看来，这或许标志着“免费时代”退潮。

限额是供需再平衡的主动选择

DeepSeek此次调整的直接背景，是需求侧的爆发式增长。据官网状态页数据，今年以来，DeepSeek出现大大小小合计57次宕机或性能下降情况。10月15日，DeepSeek发生成立以来最长时间的全局性宕机，网页端、APP、API及多个第三方接入平台全部中断，时长接近5小时。三周后的11月7日，再次发生大规模全局性宕机。

宕机的背后，并非模型技术缺陷，而是AI应用爆发带来的供需错配。工信部信息通信经济专家委员会委员盘和林对中国工业报表示，“峰值和谷值差距很大，大模型企业主要应对峰值及高并发挑战，这也是受成本约束的影响表现。”

需求增量的核心来源，是办公类AI的崛起。据QuestMobile数据，2026年9月，WorkBuddy多端合计月活3235.3万，季度环比增长647.1%；当月使用次数8.36亿次，环比增长858.4%。在办公类Agent中居首位，远超第二名百度搭子（977万）和第三名千问办公（790.5万）。自3月上线至10月底，WorkBuddy累计完成90亿次用户任务请求，词元消耗较上线初期增长50倍。WorkBuddy是腾讯旗下的办公智能体，内置混元、DeepSeek、GLM、Kimi、MiniMax等多种模型供用户自由切换，DeepSeek是其中的可选模型之一。

Harness是DeepSeek推出的独立AIAgent产品，与公众熟知的DeepSeek聊天App并非同一产品。据DeepSeekHarness官方2026年11月5日披露，截至2026年11月4日，以使用官方API的用户为统计范围，Harness月活为548万，日活为154万，日均Token消耗约92万亿。该产品于2026年8月13日推出v0.1版本，9月29日正式发布桌面客户端，上线不足三个月即达到上述规模。

办公AI本质上是集合了办公类智能体的入口。AI智能体需要拆解任务、调用工具、多轮验证、反复重读上下文，天然带来比普通对话更重的使用负载。根据Anthropic（美国人工智能安全和研究公司）的实测数据，完成一次典型智能体任务的词元消耗约为普通对话的4倍，多智能体协作下增至15倍。OpenRouter（全球最大的AI模型聚合平台）数据则显示，当下80%的词元消耗均由智能体产生。

华中伟业建设集团有限公司国际公司总经理胡双对中国工业报指出，本轮算力压力的核心增量并非普通用户闲聊对话，而是AI智能体、超长文档解析、高频次多轮办公对话等高消耗场景，造成集群高峰时段资源被击穿。

换言之，DeepSeek的限额政策，是在需求洪峰面前主动进行的供需再平衡。通过限制单次输入长度、清理沉睡对话、调控每日额度，平台得以将有限算力精准配置到更高价值的场景中。

用户使用范式走向精细化

限额政策落地后，用户会大规模迁移吗？多位专家的判断是：不会。

中国企业联合会资委会委员、高级经济师董鹏对中国工业报表示，用户会更多改变用法，而不是集体迁移。“限额像筛子，把‘全部材料丢给免费窗口’的低效用法定挤出去，推动分段处理、先摘要后精读、工具配合和人工复核；高频长文档用户会转向付费版或企业接口。”

胡双同样认为，重度办公、企业刚需用户不会大规模迁移至其他C端产品，而是主动转向官方API服务、自建RAG工作流，通过文档分块、本地预处理、结果缓存等方式降低Token消耗。“仅轻量化普通用户存在小幅迁移现象，精细化、工程化的AI使用范式成为主流。”

常信科技CEO葛林波对中国工业报指出，重度办公用户不会大规模迁移，而是拆分任务、切分上下文，适配限额规则，改变使用范式。

从“粗放投喂”到“精细调用”，这恰恰是AI工具走向成熟的标志。当用户开始学会拆分任务、优化提示词、组合工具链，AI的使用效率将显著提升，单位算力的产出价值也随之增长。限额在客观上推动了用户能力的升级，这对整个行业的健康发展是有益的。

竞争指标从用户规模到商业效率

更深层的变化在于，大模型行业的竞争逻辑正在迭代。

众多受访者认为，大模型的竞争维度正在从单一的用户规模，扩展为多维度的综合实力比拼。董鹏表示，竞争会从比用户数转向比“一次做对”、稳定和便宜。葛林波坦言：“用户量这个虚指标失效，大模型的竞争重心会转向算力调度效率、Token成本控制、Agent任务吞吐能力。”

胡双将大模型的全新核心竞争指标概括为五大维度：一是单位Token收益、客户ARPU、付费留存等商业效率指标；二是服务稳定性、故障恢复能力等SLA核心指标；三是单卡推理成本、算力调度能力等成本效率指标；四是Agent落地、长文本真实适配等场景纵深指标；五是算力供应链储备、国产算力适配、开源生态建设的长期壁垒指标。

“未来大模型赛道的竞争，不再是流量的比拼，而是算力保障、商业造血、技术落地的硬核综合实力竞争。”胡双表示。

“C端限额+B端分级”双轨模式

DeepSeek此次调整的另一看点，是其商业模式的选择：C端限额但不收费，B端API分级计价。

盘和林表示，“只要合理，重度用户会接受这套付费规则，这也是当前大部分AI模型采用的策略。”

董鹏认为，C端付费窗口不是关闭而是变窄。“免费限额是用算力换用户和反馈，企业按档收费是让高价值需求付钱、回收现金；基础免费保入口、防滥用，分级收费保稳定和服务。”

葛林波分析：“限额是筛选工具，赶走低价值高消耗羊毛党，把算力配额留给愿意在B端付费的开发者。只要B端API利润能覆盖算力成本，这套分流模式就可以长期跑通。”

胡双判断：B端分级计价、峰谷调价的商业模式逻辑扎实，但C端付费窗口并未完全关闭，未来大概率采用“基础功能永久免费、高阶场景付费订阅”的模式，平衡用户体验与算力成本。”

国产算力前景可期

董鹏表示，算力缺口主要在高峰和长文档场景，国产算力扩容能收窄峰值，但补齐要分阶段。“短期6到12个月靠限流调度、重复问题存答案、提升效率抗高峰；中期1到2年靠国产芯片集群和软件成熟明显缓解；长期2到3年靠多地调配机器和效率提升补齐。”

胡双判断：“长期算力供需将维持动态博弈状态，行业必须依靠硬件扩容叠加模型轻量化、稀疏激活等软硬件结合的方式，实现算力高效利用。”

DeepSeek的免费限额，不应被简单解读为“免费时代终结”。更准确的描述是：中国大模型行业正在告别以用户规模为唯一标尺的粗放阶段，进入以商业效率、服务稳定性、场景纵深和算力效率为核心指标的精耕时代。

针对以上中国工业报致函DeepSeek,截至发稿，对方并未回复。

【延伸阅读】

百度文心一言于2023年3月率先推出，阿里通义千问紧随其后在2023年4月上线，华为盘古在2023年7月发布，字节豆包于2023年8月推出，腾讯混元在2023年9月面世。智谱的ChatGLM同样在2023年3月开启内测。月之暗面的Kimi智能助手于2023年10月上线，以20万字长文本为切入点，是那一波中较晚但辨识度较高的产品。

DeepSeek在2025年1月发布R1模型，以推理能力打开局面。Kimi于2025年7月开源万亿参数的K2，成为国产开源模型的重要节点。智谱在2025年8月开源视觉推理模型GLM-4.5V，2026年2月发布GLM-5。腾讯混元2025年12月推出混元2.0，总参数4060B、激活32B，支持256K上下文。

据OpenRouter数据，2026年11月9日至15日这一周，中国AI大模型周调用量达119.1万亿Token，连续29周超过美国，稳居全球首位；全球调用量前四的模型全部来自中国。单一模型层面，DeepSeekV4.1Flash1017以59.2万亿Token连续第四周位居全球第一，占全平台总消耗量的28.06%，刷新单一模型份额纪录；旧版V4.1Flash另有15.5万亿，退至第三。DeepSeek本周共四款模型在榜，合计消耗80.15万亿，占平台总量的37.99%。

腾讯混元Hy4正式版以18.1万亿升至第二。智谱GLM5.3Flash以11.9万亿排在第四。

DeepSeek.content:
从英伟达换帅到DeepSeek限额：AI行业不再“拼卡”、开始“算账”

科技新知 2026-11-23 17:57:13

21384

分享到

DeepSeek 给长对话设了“7天不活跃”的门槛，英伟达在创始人离场后把投资口径调向审慎。两件事前后脚发生，却不是因果，而是同一场转向的两端：供给端开始装限速器，使用端开始清沉没占用，应用端开始追问商业闭环。算力没有变便宜，只是不再被默认可以无限追加。当“卡会越来越多”不再是前提，整个行业都得重新回答一个朴素问题：这些卡，到底为谁解决了什么问题。

几天前，向来“量大管饱”的DeepSeek突然收紧了免费额度：不再支持超过7天不活跃的长对话，每日使用量同步设限，单次输入也被压到约4万字。几乎同一时间，大西洋彼岸，一手创办英伟达的黄仁勋辞去CEO，CFO科莱特·克雷斯出任临时CEO。路透社把她描述为公司内“唯一一位与黄仁勋在AI投资上唱反调的人”，理由很具体：她曾把一项拟议中2500亿美元的OpenAI数据中心支持计划压缩到1200亿美元，被贴上“务实主义者”的标签。

把两件事并排放在一起，最容易读出的是因果，最不该读出的也是因果。DeepSeek的限额不是黄仁勋离场的直接后果。它们不是连锁反应，是同一场转向的两端：AI行业正在从“扩张逻辑”，切换到“预算逻辑”。

## 01、扩张逻辑：算力不需要踩刹车的那几年

过去几年，AI行业运行在一个 很少被明说、却无处不在的资源假设上：算力可以继续追加，扩张不需要踩刹车。

这套假设最极致的表达者是黄仁勋。他说，只要人类对智能的需求是无限的，英伟达的生意就没有天花板；英伟达本身就是一座Token工厂，大模型每一次推理、每一个Agent的思考，都在向它支付Token费，从需求端看不到尽头。2026年3月GTC上，他给出更硬的数字：Blackwell与Rubin到2027年的需求至少1万亿美元，并补了一句“实际的计算需求会比这个数字高得多”。

于是，模型公司按“卡会越来越多”做产品，数据中心按“需求会一直涨”做扩建，资本按“扩张不会停”做定价。三种角色，三套决策，共用同一个未经证明的前提。英伟达主导的从来不只是芯片供给，更是一整套关于无限扩张的行业预期——它从不证明需求，只默认需求。

而任何预期，一旦开始算账，就不再是预期，是账本。

## 02、预算逻辑：供给端装限速器，使用端清沉没账

供给端先动。新任CEO在数据中心建设上，势必不会像黄仁勋那样激进，因为财务风险被摆到 了台面中央；此前把2500亿美元的承诺压到1200亿美元，已经是一次预演。路透社引述风投人士的话说，“除了黄仁勋，没有人会像他那样积极地投资自己的客户”——这句戳中了要害：过去那轮算力扩张，有一部分不是靠终端需求撑起来的，是靠英伟达对客户的大规模融资与承诺撑起来的。当财务审慎取代扩张冲动，被抽掉的不只是一笔投资，是一种“需求可以自己造出来”的错觉。

这不是英伟达要退出AI，也不是停止卖卡。它只是作为扩张逻辑最强的那台发动机，开始给自己装限速器。

资本市场几乎同步确认了这个转向。SemiAnalysis在11月13日大幅下修AI加速器资本开支预测，理由不是供给突然消失，而是AI收入增长放缓、融资环境收紧、电力与并网约束加剧，“不计成本堆算力”的回报逻辑被重新质疑。这里需要厘清口径：被下修的是预测曲线，不是已经发生的支出；按新模型，全球AI加速器资本开支仍将从2026年约3920亿美元增至2030年的9230亿美元，方向没有逆转，只是斜率被削平。预算逻辑一旦启动，压低的是全球算力边际增速的预期，而这个预期会顺着芯片交付、租赁价格、资本开支节奏，一层层压到每一个依赖算力的模型公司。

使用端紧接着清账。回到DeepSeek，技术动因并不神秘：长对话持续累积KV缓存，闲置会话占着稀缺显存，限额是为了回收资源、保活跃用户。但技术解释只回答了“怎么砍”，没回答“为什么现在砍、砍什么、保什么”。放进预算逻辑里，取舍就非常清楚：砍闲置长对话，砍非活跃用户的沉没上下文，保活跃推理，保AGI主线；宁可让免费用户感到不便，也不急于推付费墙；宁可牺牲体验一致性，也不让算力被低效占用。这不是一次变现试探，是一次资源调度。

在中国市场，这本账还有第三个切面。全球供给预期收窄、获取海外算力的难度上升，把模型架构和国产算力绑得更深，是另一种主动的算账方式。DeepSeek V4从底层算子到通信协议、从显存调度到框架适配完成了Day 0适配，官方技术报告首次把“华为昇腾NPU”与“英伟达GPU”并列写入硬件验证清单。IDC数据显示，2026年上半年英伟达在中国数据中心AI芯片出货67.8万块，同比下降44%；昇腾从上年同期的30多万块攀升至57.2万块，份额差距收窄到6个百分点，几乎并驾齐驱。一边是别人给不了那么多了，一边是自己提前把替代路径铺好——所谓绑定不是姿态，是把供给不确定性提前折进成本里。

## 03、价值逻辑：叙事降权，应用上桌

当供给端和使用端同时开始算账，应用层的判断也会被重新排序。

这几天的APEC工商领导人峰会上，雷军说得直白：AI投入非常之大，但能够落地的场景非常有限，能真正实现商业闭环、挣到钱的公司相对较少。李彦宏给出了同向的判断：最紧迫的是找到AI真正适合的应用场景；如果企业用上AI而利润没涨，泡沫就有可能成真。

这两句话在扩张逻辑里，是正确但没人听的废话——卡还在涨，需求还在追，谁有空谈盈利？到了预算逻辑里，它们成了主旋律。卡管够的时候，没人谈盈利；需求还在追的时候，没人谈闭环；额度变成配额的时候，所有人都得谈。算力最紧张的时候，恰恰是算力叙事最需要被降权的时候。

说到底，AI的价值最终要在应用层释放。当英伟达的供给从“管够”变成“审慎”，当DeepSeek的对话从“无限”变成“配额”，行业的重心就被迫从“谁能拿到更多卡”，偏移到“谁能用有限的卡跑出真实价值”。这不是说算力不重要了，它仍然是最硬的约束之一；只是当算力不再被默认为可以无限追加，模型公司、芯片公司、应用公司都得回答一个更朴素的问题：这些卡，到底为谁解决了什么问题。

扩张时代比谁拿得多，预算时代比谁用得值。

DeepSeek.content:
# Deepseek

Deepseek serves its chat, coder, and reasoner models through an OpenAI-compatible API that you can add to LibreChat as a custom endpoint.

## Get an API key

Create a key from the Deepseek platform. Add it to your.env file:
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=your-api-key

## Configuration

Add the endpoint to thecustom list under endpoints in your librechat.yaml. If your file already has an endpoints.custom list, paste only the - name: entry into it, keeping the same indentation:
endpoints:
  custom:
    - name: "Deepseek"
      apiKey: "${DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}"
      baseURL: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
      models:
        default: ["deepseek-chat", "deepseek-coder", "deepseek-reasoner"]
        fetch: false
      titleConvo: true
      titleModel: "deepseek-chat"
      modelDisplayLabel: "Deepseek"

## Notes

- deepseek-chat and deepseek-coder work with Agents and tools.
- deepseek-reasoner, codenamed "R1," is supported and streams its thought process, but some OpenAI API parameters may not work with it. R1 can also work with Agents when tools are not used.
- deepseek-chat is the preferred model for title generation.

DeepSeek.content:
# Deepseek

Deepseek 通过 OpenAI 兼容的 API 提供其 chat、coder 和 reasoner 模型，您可以将其作为自定义 endpoint 添加到 LibreChat 中。

## 获取 API key [#get-an-api-key]

从 Deepseek platform 创建一个密钥。将其添加到你的.env 文件中：
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=your-api-key

## 配置 [#configuration]

在你的librechat.yaml 中，将 endpoint 添加到 endpoints.custom 下：
    - name: "Deepseek"
      apiKey: "${DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}"
      baseURL: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
      models:
        default: ["deepseek-chat", "deepseek-coder", "deepseek-reasoner"]
        fetch: false
      titleConvo: true
      titleModel: "deepseek-chat"
      modelDisplayLabel: "Deepseek"

## 注意事项 [#notes]

- deepseek-chat 和 deepseek-coder 可与 Agents and tools 配合使用。
- deepseek-reasoner（代号“R1”）已获得支持并可流式传输其思考过程，但某些 OpenAI API 参数可能无法与其兼容。当不使用工具时，R1 也可与 Agents 配合使用。
- deepseek-chat 是用于生成标题的首选模型。

DeepSeek.content:
# DeepSeek Harness大升级！任务时间线、代码审阅、Git插件市场齐发，小版本更新堪比V2升V3

# DeepSeek Harness大升级！任务时间线、代码审阅、Git插件市场齐发，小版本更新堪比V2升V3

2026-11-23 15:46

发布于：北京市

来源：量子位

闻乐 发自 凹非寺

量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI

DeepSeek这回更新，把网友都看愣了。

明明只是从v0.2.2升到v0.2.3-alpha.1，结果更新日志长得离谱。

DeepSeek铁粉感慨：

这帮“疯子”在0.2.2和0.2.3-alpha.1之间搞出的改动，连破坏性变更都算上，比不少软件从V2升级到V3还多。

翻开一看，还真没夸张多少，版本号是没怎么动，但更新日志确实不短……

Agent任务时间线、独立代码审阅页面、会话状态区，一口气全安排上了。

现在Agent干活，任务推进到哪一步、哪里又卡住了，都能通过任务树和进展报告查看。

代码写完也不只是甩一句「任务已完成」就交差，直接在Harness里查看代码改动，还能拉着Agent一起审。

插件市场也升级了，Git仓库可以直接作为插件来源，私有仓库里的插件照样能浏览、安装。

飞书、企业微信、钉钉等7类连接器加入，Computer Use还开始实验性支持Windows。

种种迹象都表明，DeepSeek Harness (DSH) 正在以飞快的速度，从一个Agent工具加速进化成一个完整的Agent工作平台。

Agent干到哪儿了，进度条里全有

DeepSeek这次新增了实验性时间线插件。

用过Agent的人都清楚，任务一旦复杂起来，智能体在做什么、卡在哪个环节往往会变成黑盒。

时间线插件可以沿着层级关系，展示任务及其执行状态，连Blockers（阻塞事项）都能单独记录。

某个环节无法继续推进，就能通过任务树和进展报告检查对应信息。

新版还增加了会话状态区域。

工作目录、代码变更请求、子Agent、任务和插件状态，可以集中显示。

状态区域能停靠在侧边，分区顺序也支持拖动调整。

还有个实验性的Auto review（自动审查）权限模式。

Agent每次调用受支持的工具，都可以先交给模型审查一遍。

配套还独立的Code Review代码审阅页面。

与当前用户相关的GitHub PR，可以集中放在这里查看。

PR里的修改说明、涉及文件和具体代码差异，都能直接浏览。

哪几行删掉了、哪几行新加进来，对照着看就行。

遇到拿不准的修改，还能在页面内与Agent协作审阅。

页面也支持插件扩展，开发者可以添加自己的审阅视图、代码行注解，以及工具栏和评论框中的操作入口。

GitLab同样获得支持，可以审阅和合并Merge Request。

多Agent同时修改代码时，Git Worktree也做了优化。

现在可以自定义分支名称，从远程分支创建工作树。

比如一个Agent修登录功能，另一个修改支付接口，可以分别在不同工作树里处理代码，减少相互干扰。

修改完成之后，再通过代码审阅检查。

好嘛，AI程序员现在不仅得交作业，连代码评审都安排得明明白白了。

私有Git仓库直接装插件

插件市场也没闲着。

Git仓库现在可以直接添加为插件来源，公开、私有仓库都支持。

比如一家公司自己开发了一套Agent插件。

有的负责检查内部代码规范，有的用来访问企业知识库，还有的专门处理自动化测试。

这些工具平时放在私有Git仓库里，并不准备公开。

现在可以直接把仓库添加到插件市场，让团队成员浏览、安装其中的插件。

不用为了方便安装，专门把内部工具放到公共仓库。

新增的连接器名单，也有不少熟面孔。

Linear、Notion、腾讯文档、飞书、企业微信、腾讯会议、钉钉一共7类可选插件。

可以说项目管理、知识库、协作文档、团队沟通、在线会议，平时办公用到的几类工具都照顾到了。

用户在插件页面完成账号连接或授权后，就可以在Harness对话中调用相应服务提供的工具。

连接器账号还支持统一管理，MCP加入了OAuth授权与凭据自动刷新。

当然了，工具越接越多，模型的上下文也得省着点花。

毕竟每个MCP工具都有自己的名称、参数和功能说明。

几十个工具一起加载，光是告诉模型有哪些工具可以用，就可能占掉不少Token。

于是DSH新增了可选的MCP工具按需加载模式。

需要什么工具，再加载对应的工具定义，减少模型请求中的上下文占用。

行行行，连工具说明书都开始精打细算了……

Windows电脑操作来了

更新日志再往下翻，还有一批底层调整。

首先，Windows用户终于也能上车了。

Computer Use开始实验性支持Windows。

Agent可以通过鼠标、键盘操作电脑界面，点击按钮、输入文字，还能通过cua-mcp把电脑操作能力提供给其他Agent系统调用。

macOS上的键鼠授权也进行了统一，Web连接模式则增加了远程登录。

另一边，开发者熟悉的PTC被动了刀。

Python PTC支持直接移除，Node PTC则调整为默认在多次调用之间保留变量。

底层的Cordis也升级到了4.0.0-rc.12，插件接口、工作目录参数和配置方式跟着发生了一轮变化。

已经写了自定义插件的开发者，这次升级恐怕还得顺手改改自己的代码。

v0.2.3-alpha.1刚发布，DSH同一天又跟上了v0.2.3-alpha.2，继续调整Node.js版本要求。

照这个迭代速度，估计很快还会有不少值得期待的新东西。

更新日志：

https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases#release-dsh-v0.2.3-alpha.1

参考链接：

https://x.com/teortaxesTex/status/2124437582050386001返回搜狐，查看更多
