Qwen.title: Qwen API: model IDs, thinking mode, thinking budget and errors
Qwen.description: Alibaba Cloud’s Qwen text models, including the Qwen3.8, Qwen3.7 and Qwen3.6 series, Qwen Flash and Qwen Plus. ... Qwen models are served by Alibaba Cloud Model Studio through two providers, the China site (aliyun) and the international site (alicloud), selected automatically by default.
Qwen.content:
Opens a sub-menu

# Qwen family

Alibaba Cloud’s Qwen text models, including the Qwen3.8, Qwen3.7 and Qwen3.6 series, Qwen Flash and Qwen Plus. They are called through the OpenAI-compatible API, and the Qwen3.x series also supports the Anthropic-native API. For image generation models, see Qwen-Image.

## Common tasks

## Models

For the full model list and live prices, see the model page , or query the Models API. You can omit theqwen/ prefix from model IDs.

Common model IDs (copy them exactly)

Qwen3.8 Max
qwen/qwen3.8-maxSupports image input
Qwen3.8 Flash
qwen/qwen3.8-flashSupports image input
Qwen3.7 Plus
qwen/qwen3.7-plusSupports image input
Qwen Flash
qwen/qwen-flashNo thinking by default; text only 
Capability | Supported models 
---|---
Image input | Qwen3.8 Max, 3.8 Flash, 3.8 27B, 3.7 Plus, 3.6 Flash 
Anthropic-native API | Qwen3.8, 3.7 and 3.6 series, Qwen Flash 
Responses API | Qwen3.8 and 3.7 series, Qwen Flash and others; supported_endpoints in the Models API is authoritative 

Qwen models are served by Alibaba Cloud Model Studio through two providers, the China site (aliyun) and the international site (alicloud), selected automatically by default. For how to select one, see Provider routing.

## Examples

### Python

qwen_basic.py
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.ofox.ai/v1", api_key=os.environ["OFOX_API_KEY"])

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen/qwen3.8-flash",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain idempotency in one sentence."}],
    extra_body={"enable_thinking": False},
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

## Thinking mode

Key pointThe Qwen3.x series thinks by default, and complex questions can use tens of thousands of thinking tokens and take several minutes. Turn thinking off as needed, or cap its length with thinking_budget.

Model | Default | Turn thinking off | Turn thinking on 
---|---|---|---
Qwen3.8, 3.7 and 3.6 series | On | "enable_thinking": false | On by default 
Qwen Flash, Qwen Plus | Off | Off by default | "enable_thinking": true 

In our tests on the same math problem, Qwen3.8 Flash thought for about 5,800 tokens by default and took about 1.5 minutes, while Qwen3.6 Flash thought for over 30,000 tokens and took more than 4 minutes; with thinking off, both returned within a few seconds.

### Capping thinking length

When you need thinking but want to control latency and cost, passthinking_budget (a cap on thinking tokens):

qwen_thinking_budget.py
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.ofox.ai/v1", api_key=os.environ["OFOX_API_KEY"])

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen/qwen3.8-flash",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Find all positive integers n less than 50 for which n² + n + 41 is not prime."}],
    extra_body={"enable_thinking": True, "thinking_budget": 1000},
)
msg = resp.choices[0].message
details = getattr(msg, "reasoning_details", None) or []
print("[Thinking]", "".join(d.get("text", "") for d in details)[:200], "…")
print("[Answer]", msg.content)
print("Thinking tokens:", resp.usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens)
- In our teststhinking_budget is enforced strictly: set to 200, thinking used exactly 200 tokens.
- enable_thinking and thinking_budget are not standard OpenAI SDK parameters, so put them in extra_body; when sending raw HTTP requests, put them at the top level of the request body.
- Thinking tokens are billed at the output rate; the count is inusage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens.

### Reading the thinking content

- In streaming responses, thinking content is indelta.reasoning_content, the same as the official Alibaba Cloud Model Studio API.
- In non-streaming responses, thinking content is inmessage.reasoning_details; concatenate the text of each item in order (see the example above).

## Image input

Models that support image input use the standardimage_url content block:

qwen_vision.py
import base64
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.ofox.ai/v1", api_key=os.environ["OFOX_API_KEY"])
img_b64 = base64.b64encode(open("photo.png", "rb").read()).decode()

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen/qwen3.8-flash",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [
        {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{img_b64}"}},
        {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."},
    ]}],
    extra_body={"enable_thinking": False},
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
Qwen3.7 Max, Qwen Plus and Qwen Flash are text-only; use one of the image-capable models in the table above instead.

## Use in Claude Code

The Qwen3.x series and Qwen Flash support the Anthropic-native API athttps://api.ofox.ai/anthropic:

Claude Code settings

ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
https://api.ofox.ai/anthropic
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKENPaste your OfoxAI API key

ANTHROPIC_MODEL
qwen/qwen3.8-max
- On the Anthropic API, thinking content is returned asthinking blocks.
- The Qwen3.8 series thinks a lot, so set a large enoughmax_tokens. In our tests, with max_tokens at 4000 the response could contain only a thinking block and no answer.
- Qwen Plus does not support the Anthropic API; calls returnprotocol_not_supported.

For full Claude Code setup steps, see Claude Code setup.

## JSON output and tool calling

response_format supports {"type": "json_object"} and {"type": "json_schema", ...}; tool calling uses the standard tools parameter. When using json_object, state “return JSON” and the required fields in the prompt. For the syntax, see Structured output and Function calling.

## Prompt caching

Qwen automatically caches repeated request prefixes, with no changes to your request. The cached amount is inusage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, and the cached portion is billed at the cache read rate. Caching is best-effort; requests with the same prefix may still miss.

## Common errors

Key pointSlow requests or empty answers are usually caused by thinking, which is on by default. Turn it off if you don’t need it.

HTTP · type | Error message | Cause | Fix 
---|---|---|---
400 invalid_request_error | Contains The provided messages input is invalid. The error info is [Unexpected item type in content.] | An image was sent to a text-only model (e.g. Qwen3.7 Max) | Use an image-capable model — see Image input 
400 protocol_not_supported | Model 'qwen/qwen-plus' does not support the 'anthropic' protocol on this platform. | The model does not support the Anthropic API | Use the OpenAI-compatible API, or switch to the Qwen3.x series 
404 model_not_found | Model 'qwen/qwen9-max' not found | Model ID misspelled | Copy the model ID from this page 
200, empty answer or thinking content only | — | Thinking used up the output budget | Increase max_tokens, set thinking_budget, or turn thinking off 
Request timeout | — | Thinking is on by default, and complex questions take longer | Turn thinking off, set thinking_budget, use streaming, or set the client timeout to 600 seconds or more 

For other general errors, see Error Handling.

## Official docs

The official docs describe behavior when calling Alibaba Cloud Model Studio directly. When calling through OfoxAI, model IDs and endpoints on this page take precedence.

## FAQ

How do I write a Qwen model ID?

The standard format is qwen/qwen3.8-flash; you can also omit the qwen/ prefix.

How do I turn off Qwen thinking?

Pass "enable_thinking": false; with the OpenAI SDK, put it in extra_body. The Qwen3.8, 3.7 and 3.6 series think by default; Qwen Flash and Qwen Plus do not.

Why does Qwen take several minutes to respond?

The Qwen3.x series thinks by default, and complex questions can use tens of thousands of thinking tokens. Turn thinking off, or cap its length with thinking_budget, e.g. "thinking_budget": 1000.

How do I use Qwen thinking_budget?

Pass it together with "enable_thinking": true; the value is the cap on thinking tokens, e.g. 1000. In our tests it is enforced strictly.

Which Qwen models can understand images?

Qwen3.8 Max, 3.8 Flash, 3.8 27B, 3.7 Plus and 3.6 Flash support image input. Qwen3.7 Max, Qwen Plus and Qwen Flash are text-only.

Can I use Qwen in Claude Code?

Yes. Set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to https://api.ofox.ai/anthropic and use a Qwen3.x series model such as qwen/qwen3.8-max. Qwen Plus does not support the Anthropic API.

Where is Qwen reasoning_content?

In streaming responses it is in delta.reasoning_content; in non-streaming responses it is in message.reasoning_details, where you concatenate the text of each item.

## 阿里新一代大模型曝光，全球开发者抢测Qwen4！

新智元 整合编辑：太平洋科技 发布于：2026-11-23 17:33

由华为云驱动

2026年11月，阿里巴巴发布Qwen4-Max预览版，全球开发者抢先体验。这款国产大模型在知识理解、3D场景构建及复杂编程上表现出色，吸引众多海外用户热议。Qwen4以其高效细节处理和文化内涵引发广泛关注，被视为本地部署潜力巨大。此次发布为AI技术发展掀起新热潮，业内期待其全量上线。

最近，一个国产大模型，在全球开发者社区掀起了一场大狂欢！

让人出乎意料的是，这个模型还没正式上线。

它，就是阿里今天刚刚发布预览版的Qwen 4-Max。

之前圈内大V激动地预告：这是爆炸性的一周，Fable 5.5、GPT-6.2 Sol、Gemini Kryptom都要来了，Qwen 4也要登场！

是的，海外开发者已经把Qwen 4放进了和O/A两家新模型同等重要的期待名单中。

抢先实测，效果惊艳

和以往不同，本次Qwen采用极简式发布，只是在官号上讲述了一下预览版的性能和接入Agent：对知识理解更深入，世界感知更立体，Coding与Agentic能力也持续进阶。擅长复杂编程、专业办公、前端设计和专业软件操作。

今日起，Qwen4-Max预览版首发上线阿里TokenPlan，限时最低1折即可体验Qwen4模型。千问办公、Qoder、千问APP、QwenStudio等也可第一时间体验。

我们也在预览版公开后，第一时间接入Codex抢先体验了下，交回来的《灰烬地城》，第一眼就把我们惊到了！

披着斗篷的探险者举起火把，暖光铺在斑驳的石砖上，木箱、红旗和厚重墙体，把地牢的空间层次撑了起来。

镜头前的墙面还做了切开处理，让人物和房间结构清楚地露出来，血条、钥匙、宝箱计数也各就各位，细节颇有游戏开发的章法。

看到这份画面答卷，就能理解外网开发者为什么如此兴奋了——光看这个架势，就想接过键盘，去拐角后面探探路。

物理特性极度逼真，如此复杂、清晰、符合逻辑的画面，让我们直呼太强了！

除了《灰烬地城》，我们还用Qwen4跑了另一个Case，效果同样优秀！

这台《六颗星的旅行》，第一眼就有高级机械艺术品的质感。

胡桃木支架的沉稳色泽、黄铜轨道的暖金反光、玻璃弹珠的透亮光泽，各有各的味道。

连支架上的金属箍、提升机的链条，以及底板上交错的投影都做得细致，整个画面精致得让人想多转几个角度看看。

小球的运动同样舒服：沿轨道滚落、转弯、经过分流，再被提升机送回高处，整个过程衔接自然，运动有重量感，机械传动也有清楚的节奏。

看着几颗弹珠在层层轨道间循环穿梭，还真有点上瘾，简直停不下来。

更讨喜的是，点中一颗弹珠，镜头就能跟着它沿轨道「旅行」，近距离欣赏这套机械的运转；还能自由旋转视角、控制提升机启停。

材质、细节、运动和交互都照顾到了，Qwen交出的这件小作品，完成度确实让人眼前一亮。

不止我们觉得，很多海外网友也表示，Qwen4的能力比起前一代更强了。

「北冥有鱼」，让老外连夜翻查中国神话

之所以Qwen4这次能在海外引起超高关注，一切的起点，源于上周五Qwen官方发布的一张神秘海报。

海报上只有一句古诗词：「北冥有鱼，其名为_」，下面是一行英文：The becoming begins.

对中国开发者来说，这句《庄子·逍遥游》的话简直是刻在DNA里的。

「鲲」的发音，恰好与Qwen（千问）同音。

才过不久，二创就满天飞了。

甚至，不少海外开发者为了解开彩蛋，居然去连夜搜起了庄子、逍遥游和中国神话。

一位波兰开发者做的科普

一个大模型预热，被玩出了一波文化输出，太硬核了。

手搓整个3D世界？Qwen4 demo惊艳海外开发者

其实，早前Qwen4泄露的demo，早就惊艳了一大波开发者。

拿到内测资格的用户，纷纷晒出Qwen4在真实场景下的超强能力。

@loktar00 使用内测的Qwen4 preview，结合Qwen Code，直接「手搓」出了一座地下城城堡！

跑完20万token，就达到了这种完成度，网友直言：Qwen4这波稳了！

有人说，要是后续小模型能做到这个程度，本地部署要起飞了。

Loktar还放出了用纯vanilla.js和three.js生成的灯塔横截面，以及水面光影效果。

他评价说：「Qwen4用极少的token实现了更高的效率，水和光影的效果太棒了，进步太大了！」

@intheworldofai 用Qwen4花了2小时53分钟（Max thinking），直接复刻了一个类似《我的世界》的3D游戏雏形！

游戏中的一切都是Qwen4写的，他的体感是——「有时像是自己在用Fable 5」。

开发者 @leo114119 花了两个小时，用Qwen4生成了一个美国白宫的3D建模。

「68个房间，每一个都可以进去，建模效果非常惊艳！如果这只是Qwen4 27B，那实在是相当不错了！」

在像素风的海岛小镇骑自行车的鹈鹕，效果有点惊艳。

博主 @xiax0603 做了个测试：让Qwen4与Gemini 4 Hydrogen (Flash) 各自生成一段3D火箭发射回收动画。

2小时8分钟生出来的视频令人惊喜，唯一的缺点可能就是速度太慢。

以下，是更多惊艳demo。

有人直言——Qwen4-27B将是单卡部署战力天花板。

中国AI模型，成为全球开发者心头好

从Qwen2.5的异军突起，到如今Qwen4的「未见其人，先听其声」，阿里Qwen能让全球开发者瞩目，靠的就是一个实力。

说起来，这两天的AI圈有多卷？昨天是Fable 5.2在秀肌肉，今天是全面解禁的Gemini 4 Carbon来炸场。

从这次体验来看，Qwen4-Max预览版虽比不上前两者，但在复杂编程、3D场景构建和交互设计上，还是展现出了不错的完成度。

比如，地下城的空间层次、弹珠机械的运动逻辑，以及材质、光影和操作细节，让我们直观看到了它理解需求、编写代码和处理细节的能力。

当然，除了生成好看的场景，我们还很好奇正式发布的Qwen4版本，能否在更复杂的项目里持续修改、排查问题，把功能一步步做完整。

Qwen4-Max，别藏着掖着了，赶紧全量上线吧，全村人都等着开席呢！

# 阿里云最新 Qwen3.7-Plus 科普：模型定位、功能特征、综合能力、应用场景、计费拆解

2026-11-23 12

举报

简介： Qwen3.7-Plus 的定位很聪明：它不去争"最强"，而是把"文本＋视觉＋智能体"三样都保住，把价格压在中档。它的成本设计也很有特点——256K 分档、缓存命中 0.2 元、Batch 半价，三条杠杆用好了，实际单价比标价低一大截。判断该不该用它，只需回答一个问题：**你的业务是"要看着屏幕干活"，还是"只要读文字答题"？** 前者它是当前性价比最优解，后者往上走 Max、往下走 Flash 都更合适。

模型选型最难的从来不是"最强的是哪个"，而是"够用的那个在哪"。旗舰模型能力拉满，但贵；轻量模型便宜，但复杂任务撑不住。真正被大量业务用起来的，往往是中间那一档。

Qwen3.7-Plus 就是这一档。它是 Qwen3.7 系列里主打高性价比的 Plus 模型，模型 IDqwen3.7-plus，当前能力等同于快照版 qwen3.7-plus-2026-05-26。它的特别之处在于：在文本能力之上补齐了视觉，同时保住了智能体能力——这不是"缩水版旗舰"，而是"另一种取向的全能选手"。下面完整介绍。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

### 参考阿里云主流云产品大全：

云产品 | 核心功能 | 适配人群  
---|---|---
轻量应用服务器专区： https://t.aliyun.com/U/CENIbY | 主打开箱即用，自带系统镜像和常见建站模板，操作门槛极低 | 适合新手、个人用户做博客、静态站、短期测试  
ECS 云服务器专区： https://t.aliyun.com/U/Rh9d1U | 标准云算力实例，支持完整VPC专有网络、弹性网卡、安全组精细配置 | 个人开发者、中小企业正式业务、长期部署项目 
GPU 云服务器专区： https://t.aliyun.com/U/TuZffa | 深度优化的GPU算力为模型推理、图形处理提供更强性能支持 | 个人开发者、中小企业 
最新阿里云优惠券领取入口 https://t.aliyun.com/U/Mfieow | 全品类代金券领取、120+款云产品专属折扣，享优惠折上折 | 个人开发者、中小企业 
百炼大模型服务专区： https://t.aliyun.com/U/2Nuy7H | 千问 AI Token Plan 低至5折 | 个人开发者、中小企业 

## 一、模型定位：多模态交互的混合智能体

官方定位有一句关键表述："其核心特色为多模态交互混合智能体能力"。往下一句展开是四项能力：感知真实世界场景、读取屏幕并操作 GUI、基于视觉参考生成代码、端到端导航移动应用。

这四项合起来，画像就非常清楚了——它不是"会看图说话的聊天模型"，而是"能看着屏幕干活的操作者"。

把它放进 3.7 系列的三档里，位置一目了然：

档位 | 取向 | 典型用途 
---|---|---
Qwen3.7-Max | 规模最大、综合能力最强 | 最难的推理与长周期自主执行 
Qwen3.7-Plus | 性价比、多模态＋智能体 | 日常业务主力、屏幕与 GUI 类任务 
Qwen3.7-Flash | 轻量、低延迟 | 高并发、简单任务 

一个务实判断：Plus 是"能覆盖 80% 业务"的那一档，Max 留给真正啃不动的硬任务，Flash 留给量大且简单的调用。

关键规格先摆出来：

指标 | 数值 
---|---
上下文长度 | 1,000,000 Token 
最大输入（常规） | 991,808 
最大输入（思考模式） | 983,616 
最大输出 | 131,072（128K） 
最大思维链 | 262,144（256K） 
输入模态 | 文本、图像 
输出模态 | 文本 
模式 | 非思考 / 思考 
视觉能力 | 全面升级的视觉-语言能力 

## 二、核心特征

第一，视觉能力是升级重点。 官方原话是"在强大文本能力的基础上全面升级了视觉-语言能力"。这条对 Plus 档意义很大——过去"便宜的那一档"通常牺牲多模态，现在不用了。

第二，完整的智能体能力。 编码、工具使用、生产力工作流三项能力全部保留。这意味着它不仅能对话，还能规划、调工具、多步执行。

第三，屏幕与 GUI 操作。 "读取屏幕并操作 GUI"是最有想象力的一条。它的应用形态是：截图进来，模型理解界面结构，输出下一步该点哪里、该填什么。做 RPA 替代、做自动化测试、做无障碍辅助，都靠这条。

第四，基于视觉参考生成代码。 给一张设计稿或界面截图，直接产出代码。这是"设计到实现"链路里最省人力的一环。

第五，端到端导航移动应用。 官方表述是"端到端导航移动应用"——理解应用界面并完成操作流程。对 App 自动化测试、跨应用流程编排有价值。

第六，双模式与超长思维链。 支持非思考与思考两种模式，思考模式思维链上限 262,144 Token。这个预算足够做很深的多步推理，而不至于被截断。

第七，百万上下文。 上下文 1M，装得下整库代码、整套文档。但这里埋着一个成本陷阱，见计费部分。

## 三、能力拆解：能做好什么，做不好什么

做得好：

- 界面自动化：读屏、定位控件、生成操作步骤。
- 设计稿转代码：截图进、代码出，前端提效明显。
- 长文档处理：百万上下文装整套材料。
- 编码与工具调用：完整智能体链路，多步任务可编排。
- 图文混合问答：图表、票据、报表的结构化理解。
- 生产力工作流：批量摘要、字段抽取、格式化改写。
- 移动应用流程导航：跨页面操作理解。

不擅长或需要注意的：

- 需要极致推理上限的硬任务（交给 Max）；
- 需要亚秒级响应的海量简单调用（交给 Flash）；
- 需要模型直接输出语音或图像（它只输出文本）；
- 需要一次性处理超过百万上下文的材料（物理上限）；
- 需要"看完视频就操作"——输入以图像为主，视频能力不在其位。

一个必须提前想清楚的问题：GUI 操作的可靠性边界。 模型输出的是"坐标/元素描述/操作步骤"，实际点击是客户端做的。界面改版、弹窗、加载延迟，都会让结果漂移。所以这条能力适合做"半自动"——模型给建议、人做确认，而不是全自动无人值守。

## 四、适用场景

场景 | 关键能力 | 说明 
---|---|---
界面自动化/RPA | 屏幕读取、GUI 操作 | 建议保留人工确认 
设计稿转前端代码 | 视觉参考生成代码 | 截图＋需求描述 
自动化测试脚本生成 | 界面理解、编码 | 配合测试框架 
长文档分析与摘要 | 百万上下文 | 注意 256K 计费分档 
智能客服/助手 | 工具调用、视觉 | 多模态问答 
表单与票据识别 | 视觉理解 | 输出结构化需后处理 
科研与知识工作 | 思考模式、长思维链 | 深推理任务 
高并发简单问答 | — | 改用 Flash 更划算 

## 五、计费与优惠：分档计价，这是重点

计费单位为元/百万 Token，按"单次请求的输入 Token 范围"分两档：

计费项 | 输入 ≤ 256K | 256K < 输入 ≤ 1M 
---|---|---
输入 | 2 元 | 6 元 
输出 | 8 元 | 24 元 
输入（隐式缓存命中） | 0.4 元 | 1.2 元 
显式缓存创建 | 2.5 元 | 7.5 元 
显式缓存命中 | 0.2 元 | 0.6 元 
输入（Batch File） | 1 元 | 3 元 
输出（Batch File） | 4 元 | 12 元 
输入（Batch Chat） | 2 元 | 6 元 
输出（Batch Chat） | 8 元 | 24 元 

另有限时 8 折活动价（以控制台实时展示为准），折算后常规档输入约 1.6 元、输出约 6.4 元；国际地域（新加坡、法兰克福、弗吉尼亚、东京）价格另列，以官方页为准。

五个必须记住的结论：

第一，256K 是道分水岭，跨过去单价乘三。 不是"超出部分涨价"，而是整单按高档计价。一次请求塞 300K，全部按 6 元/24 元算。

第二，所以"拆"比"塞"便宜。 算个账：一次请求 300K 输入，输出 20K——

- 单次（超档）：0.3×6 ＋ 0.02×24 ＝ 1.8 ＋ 0.48 ＝ 2.28 元
- 拆成两次 150K（常规档）：2×(0.15×2) ＋ 0.02×8 ＝ 0.6 ＋ 0.16 ＝ 0.76 元

同样的信息量，拆开只要三分之一。前提是拆分点切在语义完整处。

第三，显式缓存命中是全表最便宜的价。 0.2 元，是常规输入价（2 元）的十分之一。固定知识库、固定系统提示、固定长文档，走显式缓存能把输入成本压到极低——这是长期业务最该优化的地方。

第四，Batch File 直接半价。 输入 1 元、输出 4 元，是常规档的一半。批量离线任务（夜间跑批、日志分析、批量摘要）走 Batch 最划算。

第五，输出永远比输入贵四倍。 2 : 8 的比例说明成本主要在"生成"侧。控制max_tokens、要求要点式输出，比压输入更有效。

省钱五个实招：

- 守住 256K 线：单请求输入控制在此之下，超长任务拆分。
- 显式缓存打底：稳定前缀一律缓存，命中价 0.2 元。
- 批量任务走 Batch File：半价，且不占实时配额。
- 按任务选模式：简单任务关掉思考，省思维链输出费。
- 输出限长：明确要求结构化或要点式，避免长篇散文。

## 六、接入示例

基础对话（非思考模式）：
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["DASHSCOPE_API_KEY"],
    base_url="[https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1](https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1)",
)
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen3.7-plus",
    messages=[
        {
   "role": "system", "content": "<固定知识库放这里，利于命中缓存>"},
        {
   "role": "user", "content": "把这份需求拆成可执行的开发任务清单"},
    ],
    max_tokens=4096,           # 输出 8 元/百万，务必限长
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

          AI 代码解读

思考模式（深度推理任务）：
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen3.7-plus",
    messages=[{
   "role": "user", "content": "分析这套架构的三个单点故障，给出验证方案"}],
    extra_body={
   "enable_thinking": True},   # 思维链上限 262,144
    max_tokens=8192,
)

          AI 代码解读

视觉输入（截图转代码 / 界面理解）：
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen3.7-plus",
    messages=[{
   "role": "user", "content": [
        {
   "type": "text", "text": "按这张设计稿生成页面代码，用 Tailwind"},
        {
   "type": "image_url", "image_url": {
   "url": "[https://example.com/ui.png](https://example.com/ui.png)"}},
    ]}],
)

          AI 代码解读

接入前先做一次 Token 估算，避免无意中跨档：
def rough_tokens(text_cn: str, img_count: int = 0) -> int:
    # 粗估：中文约 1 字 ≈ 1 Token，图像按分辨率折算，务必用官方 tokenizer 校准
    return len(text_cn) + img_count * 1000

          AI 代码解读

## 七、使用注意事项

第一，先看"单次输入"再谈单价。跨 256K 整单涨价，接入前把长任务拆好，别让一次请求拖垮预算。

第二，思考模式的输入上限略低。常规 991,808，思考模式 983,616——差得不多，但卡在上限边缘的长任务要留意。

第三，显式缓存的创建也要花钱。创建 2.5 元/百万，命中 0.2 元/百万。只有"同一前缀会被反复使用"时才值得建。

第四，GUI 操作要做降级方案。界面改版、动态加载、弹窗都可能让模型判断失效，必须有人工兜底或失败重试。

第五，视觉任务要先控图。图片分辨率越高，Token 消耗越大；能裁切到关键区域就别整屏送。

第六，处理设计稿、界面截图、内部文档时，注意数据分级与授权范围；能力可用不等于内容可外传。

## 结语

Qwen3.7-Plus 的定位很聪明：它不去争"最强"，而是把"文本＋视觉＋智能体"三样都保住，把价格压在中档。它的成本设计也很有特点——256K 分档、缓存命中 0.2 元、Batch 半价，三条杠杆用好了，实际单价比标价低一大截。判断该不该用它，只需回答一个问题：你的业务是"要看着屏幕干活"，还是"只要读文字答题"？ 前者它是当前性价比最优解，后者往上走 Max、往下走 Flash 都更合适。

Qwen.description: 阿里巴巴正式发布拥有2.4万亿个参数的Qwen4-Max人工智能模型。 阿里巴巴推出拥有 2.4 万亿个参数的 Qwen4-Max，在编程、推理和自动化方面表现出色，同时降低了使用成本并提高了安全性。
Qwen.content:
# 阿里巴巴正式发布拥有2.4万亿个参数的Qwen4-Max人工智能模型。

阿里巴巴推出拥有 2.4 万亿个参数的 Qwen4-Max，在编程、推理和自动化方面表现出色，同时降低了使用成本并提高了安全性。

总部位于杭州的电子商务和科技巨头阿里巴巴集团近日发布了Qwen4-Max人工智能模型。该模型经过训练，能够存储可用于检测和修复软件漏洞的网络安全知识，同时还能清除旨在增强网络攻击能力的内容。

阿里巴巴发布了Qwen4-Max，这是迄今为止Qwen产品线中最强大的型号。Qwen4-Max拥有2.4万亿个参数、原生图像识别功能以及百万级上下文窗口，能够出色地完成工作、创意和研究等众多领域的复杂任务。

Qwen4-Max 在顶级性能测试中名列前茅，尤其是在编程、自动化任务和视觉推理方面。它在 Code Arena（一个实用编程排名）中排名第六，并在代理工作流程、工作效率和视觉推理等专项测试中得分很高，例如 Agents' Last Exam、Vals Index、JobBench 和 Chartography。

根据 Work360 的专有基准测试（该基准测试评估 721 个专业领域中复杂行业任务的性能），Qwen4-Max 的性能优于其前代产品 Qwen3.8-Max。该模型在高强度推理模式下使用的令牌数量减少了 35%，并且每个任务的平均成本降低了约 60%。

这些改进得益于新的 Qwen4 架构，该架构在注意力方面、冗余连接和嵌入方面升级了稀疏混合专家 (MoE) 设计。

Qwen4-Max 构建为 MoE 模型，总共有 2.4 万亿个参数，每个代币仅激活 710 亿个参数，比相同规模（2.4 万亿）的 Qwen3.8-Max 少激活 25%，以更低的推理成本提供更强大的功能。

Qwen4-Max现已通过代币包和API在QwenCloud上线。用户还可以通过阿里巴巴旗下平台（包括QwenWork和QwenStudio）访问该模型。准入费用（隐式缓存命中）为每百万个代币0.075美元。

美国和中国都在竞相开发功能日益强大的人工智能系统，但现在都面临着日益增长的安全风险。

人们担心这项技术可能会被利用来进行网络攻击、开发危险武器或不受人类控制地运行——这种情况有时被描述为“叛逆的人工智能”。

阿里巴巴在中国的竞争对手腾讯和登月科技都已宣布了安全保障措施，这表明市场正朝着更加透明的方向发展。

此前，SemiAnalysis 在 10 月份发布的一份报告显示，中国领先的人工智能开发商仅公布了已发布的 857 个模型中 3.6% 的安全测试结果。

本月，腾讯表示，已将其新款 Hy4 机型的网络安全培训限制在防御目的范围内；而 Moonshot 在 10 月份表示，已有意降低其 Kimi K3.1 Pro 机型的网络攻击能力。

阿里巴巴表示，该型号产品还能提供更强的化学、生物、放射性和核威胁防护。他们还补充说，内部审查并未发现任何证据表明该型号产品能够显著提升用户执行危险任务的能力。

该公司计划发布 Qwen4 系列的更小、开源的模型，允许世界各地的开发者下载和修改它们。

GLM.content:
GLM-5.3 is now available to all GLM Coding Plan users, with 50% better coding performance! Subscribe now

Overview

GLM-5.3 is Z.ai’s latest flagship model, delivering comprehensive advancements in complex software engineering and agent capabilities. It uses the same base model as GLM-5.2, with all improvements driven by post-training. Compared with GLM-5.2, it delivers significantly stronger performance in complex programming and long-horizon tasks:Stronger Coding CapabilityGLM-5.3 delivers a significant improvement in coding capabilities, achieving a 50% performance gain over GLM-5.2 on Z.ai Code Bench. It also reaches state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance among open-source models on public benchmarks, including Terminal Bench 3.0 and Agents’ Last Exam (CLI).Emergent Cyber CapabilityAs the scale of post-training continues to expand, the model’s cybersecurity capabilities have improved at a rate that exceeds expectations. GLM-5.3 achieves the best performance to date on the CyberGym vulnerability discovery benchmark. Moreover, the deeper it progresses along the vulnerability exploitation chain, the more pronounced its gains over GLM-5.2 become, with scores on vulnerability exploitation benchmarks exceeding twice those of GLM-5.2.↗ Blog

Feature Changes

GLM-5.3 currently supports text-only inputs, with a 1M-token context window and a maximum output length of 128K tokens. GLM-5.3 always operates with reasoning enabled and supports three reasoning effort levels: low, high, and max. Disabling reasoning is no longer supported. The reasoning parameters are described below:

Parameter

Values

Default

Description

thinking.type

enabled

enabled

Supports reasoning only; disabling reasoning is not supported.

Migration Notice: If your application currently uses thinking.type: "disabled", please change it to enabled and set reasoning_effort to low before updating the model ID to glm-5.3. Otherwise, the request will fail.

For complex tasks such as coding, we recommend using max. An example is provided below:

If you have previously subscribed to a GLM Coding Plan, including an expired subscription, you can currently access the model API only through the OpenAI Chat Completion-compatible protocol. We will continue to improve and optimize this in upcoming iterations.

GLM Coding Plan

GLM-5.3 is now fully available, and you can use it with your preferred coding agents. GuideThe new GLM Coding Plan adopts a points-based quota system, providing transparent and predictable usage. Model calls made during off-peak hours, including all day on weekends, consume only 50% of the standard points. Subscribe now: Individual Plan、Team Plan.

Capability Support

Thinking Mode：Provides multiple thinking modes to accommodate different task requirements

Streaming Messages：Supports real-time streaming responses for an enhanced user interaction experience

Function Calling：Provides powerful tool-calling capabilities and supports integration with a wide range of external tools

Context Caching：Uses an intelligent caching mechanism to optimize performance in long-context conversations

Structured Output：Supports structured output formats such as JSON for seamless system integration

Key Advancements

GLM-5.3 delivers significant improvements across complex software engineering, terminal operations, and a broader range of real-world Agent tasks.LLM Performance Evaluation

For GLM-5.3, we pushed environment scaling toward tasks that look less like coding exercises and more like real units of expert work. The environments now cover a much broader range of production workflows, with tasks designed around how engineering and research work is actually carried out in practice. Some represent several days of work for an experienced engineer.In an ML infrastructure task, for example, the model may be given the same working environment as an engineer, with access to compute clusters, storage systems, internal documentation, codebases, and experiment results. It must diagnose bottlenecks across the training stack, implement optimizations, run experiments, and deliver a measurable end-to-end speedup while preserving correctness. Training on environments at this level pushes the model toward taking ownership of substantial work end to end, rather than relying on users to decompose the problem and supervise each step.As agent capability improves, much of the difficulty in scaling post-training moves from the model to the environment. A useful task environment has to be executable, verifiable, and close to real professional work — and we need many of them, not a handful of hand-built ones. To scale this process, we built pipelines that synthesize environments end to end, and for a subset of tasks, the RL reward signal as well. Research agents collect task patterns from real work and turn them into runnable long-horizon environments with multi-step dependencies and hidden state; a judge agent then attempts each task to verify that it is actually solvable. Verifiers are synthesized without access to the reference solution, while solver trajectories are used to discover and close reward shortcuts. A verifier that passes oracle, no-op, and unsolved-state checks produces a binary reward reliable enough to train on directly.It carries over the RL strategies introduced in GLM-5.2, including SAO with compaction, which helps these gains hold on long-horizon tasks rather than only on short ones. The effect shows up across both coding and general agent tasks. GLM-5.3 improves from 4.6 to 28.3 on Terminal-Bench 3.0, from 46.2 to 66.9 on DeepSWE v1.1, and from 23.8 to 28.5 on Agents’ Last Exam. These pipelines still require a meaningful amount of human-in-the-loop work; making environment generation and verification more autonomous is one of the next steps.Beyond public benchmarks, we introduce Z.ai Code Bench, an in-house benchmark designed to evaluate coding agents under realistic user scenarios. It covers diverse task categories and places agents in complex local development environments. At different effort levels, we evaluate agents along two dimensions: end-to-end task completion rate and fine-grained checklist accuracy. As a private benchmark, Z.ai Code Bench also reduces the risk of contamination from public test sets and gives us a more faithful measure of real-world user experience.# Agentic Coding Performance by Effort Level

Z.ai Code Bench v1.0, evaluated on Claude Code 2.1.207

As shown in the figure, GLM-5.3 improves both performance and token efficiency. It delivers markedly stronger agentic coding results than GLM-5.2 at every effort level while consuming fewer output tokens. At Max effort, GLM-5.3 reaches 34.5% at roughly 75K output tokens per task, compared with 23.4% at 96K for GLM-5.2. The same shift holds against closed models. At High effort, GLM-5.3 reaches 31.4% at around 50K output tokens, surpassing Claude Opus 4.8 at 29.5% with 120K. GLM-5.3 remains behind Claude Fable 5, which reaches 39.5% at Max effort.

Emergent Cyber Capability

As part of post-training, we introduced vulnerability discovery data and environments into the training mix. We expected this to make the model better at finding and reasoning about vulnerabilities. What surprised us was how quickly the capability continued to develop as training scaled. GLM-5.3 did not simply become better at identifying isolated flaws: it began to reason across multiple stages of exploitation, forming coherent plans for complete exploitation chains.We evaluate GLM-5.3 across three benchmarks covering different stages of vulnerability analysis and exploitation.CyberSecurityEvaluation

On CyberGym, which starts from white-box source code and tests whether the model can identify and validate vulnerabilities by triggering faults, GLM-5.3 scores 84.5%, up from GLM-5.2’s 77.2% — the best result on the benchmark, ahead of Mythos 5 (83.8%) and GPT-5.6 Sol (83.6%). On ExploitBench, which requires deeper reasoning about real vulnerabilities and their exploitation, GLM-5.3 reaches 54.4%, more than doubling GLM-5.2’s 24.4%, while Mythos 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol score 78.0% and 76.5%, respectively. On ExploitGym, which measures how many exploitation tasks a model can complete under time-normalized budgets, GLM-5.3 completes 105 tasks within two hours and 130 within six hours, compared with 29 and 39 for GLM-5.2; budgets are normalized across models using per-model throughput figures, detailed in the footnotes. Mythos 5 remains well ahead at 181 and 247 tasks.The pattern across the three is consistent: the further up the exploitation chain a benchmark sits, the larger the gain from GLM-5.2 — and also the wider the remaining gap to the closed frontier. Capability is growing fastest exactly where we are furthest behind.We then tested whether these capabilities transfer beyond controlled benchmarks. Since GLM-5.2, we have been working with several security teams in China to run our models against real-world codebases. After expert review, screening, and deduplication, the model identified 2,436 vulnerabilities across 269 projects, including 1,097 medium-to-high severity issues. The findings span system kernels, operating systems, browser engines, open-source infrastructure, web applications, and network protocols. Many had remained unnoticed for years or even decades, with the oldest dating back roughly 40 years.This work has since grown into an ongoing disclosure effort. Overview

GLM-5.4 is Z.ai’s latest flagship model and the first built on the Loop Transformer architecture, reaching intelligence levels comparable to 2T-3T parameter models. It marks the start of Generalized Coding, where code becomes the foundation for solving a much wider range of tasks and unlocking new capabilities:Loop Transformer ArchitectureGLM-5.4 introduces a Loop Transformer architecture that reuses 28 layers of the GLM-5 base model across two iterations, enabling deeper reasoning without increasing parameter count. Combined with optimized KV caching and sparse attention, it delivers stronger reasoning performance while keeping deployment costs under control, particularly at 1M context lengths.Generalized CodingDriven by improvements in both coding and vision, GLM-5.4 generalizes well beyond traditional software development. It can write code to generate and edit videos, build complete games, and handle 3D modeling and mechanical design.↗ Blog

How to Use

GLM Coding Plan

GLM-5.4 is now available to all GLM Coding Plan users and can be accessed through your preferred coding tools. For users on weekly quota plans, the available quota for GLM-5.4 is increased to 1.5× that of GLM-5.3.Subscribe Now: Personal Plan, Team Plan.

Capability Support

Thinking Mode：Supports thinking mode for deeper reasoning; with the Loop Transformer, the model reasons more deeply without adding parameters, and part of the reasoning shifts from explicit output tokens into the implicit depth of the loop

Streaming Messages：Supports real-time streaming responses for an enhanced user interaction experience, with up to 200 tokens/s during off-peak hours and 70–80 tokens/s at peak load

Function Calling：Provides powerful tool-calling capabilities and supports integration with a wide range of external tools

Context Caching：Uses an intelligent caching mechanism to optimize performance in long-context conversations

Structured Output：Supports structured output formats such as JSON for seamless system integration

Key Advancements

Over the past three months, we have aggressively scaled both loop depth and model size in parallel. The first surprise came from the Loop Transformer architecture itself. By executing a shared block of layers across multiple iterations, the model can reason more deeply without adding parameters, effectively matching the performance of much larger models.GLM-5.4 is our first flagship model built on the Loop Transformer architecture, reaching intelligence levels comparable to 2T-3T parameter models.GLM-5.4 marks the start of Generalized Coding, where code becomes the foundation for solving a much wider range of tasks and unlocking new capabilities.The model still has some limitations. Most notably, it tends to get caught in overly long “marathon thinking” loops, though this prolonged reflection and self-correction does consistently improve accuracy beyond its parameter count.# GLM-5.4 Win Rate

The Loop Architecture

As we noted in our GLM-5.3 technical blog, memory-intensive tasks benefit from more parameters, while reasoning-intensive tasks benefit from more effective compute. Large-scale software engineering, cybersecurity, 3D modeling, and physical control are all ultra-long-chain reasoning tasks. The model must follow multi-step causal chains while maintaining global logical consistency. Stacking parameters and memorizing data cannot solve this.

From Pre-Trained Base to Loop Transformer

In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count.The idea is not new. The 2018 Universal Transformer proposed weight-shared depth, and recent work on recurrent depth and looped language models has shown gains at small scales. However, while weight sharing improves parameter efficiency, looped models trained from scratch still lag behind unshared models under the same pre-training compute budget. Instead of pre-training from scratch, we adapted an already pre-trained base model into a Loop Transformer through continued training. This lets us raise the intelligence ceiling with a relatively small compute overhead.

Architectural Modifications at 750B Scale

GLM-5.4 loops 28 layers of the GLM-5 base model for two iterations. To balance performance gains with deployment costs at the 750B scale, we made three changes after extensive experimentation:

Gated Progressive Updates

When converting middle layers of an existing model into a multi-pass loop, directly overwriting hidden states causes activation norms to blow up across iterations. Downstream layers then receive representations outside their expected scale and distribution.GLM-5.4 adds independent per-token gates for each iteration to proportionally write candidate updates back into the residual stream. After training, these gates develop a clear division of labor. The first pass builds global context and writes conservatively with small gate values to keep scales stable. The second pass reuses this state to refine the output, opening the gates to write full updates. The gates also adjust step size dynamically based on token difficulty: on harder tokens, the first pass writes more aggressively so complex predictions benefit more from iterative refinement.

A naive implementation keeps a full KV cache for every loop iteration, multiplying memory usage with the loop count. Instead, we build on cross-loop KV sharing by supplementing it with a local sliding window for the new pass: the second loop reuses the sparse KV selected in the first pass, while retaining its own newly generated KV within the sliding window. These two KV streams can overlap at the same positions, allowing the model to attend to both the first-pass context representations and the updated local representations from the second pass.As a result, an extra loop only costs one sliding window of KV cache rather than a full context cache. At 1M context lengths, this keeps GLM-5.4’s deployment cost increase over GLM-5.3 well under control.

Sparse Attention Index Reuse

GLM-5.4’s base model uses sparse attention. The second loop directly reuses the attention indices generated by the first loop’s indexer, adding zero indexing overhead. Our experiments show this performs nearly identically to recomputing indices on every pass.

Looping is also a strict test of Scaling Correctness: any architectural change must still work at scale. Before committing our flagship model to it, we validated the Loop architecture progressively across 1B, 4B, 30B, and 750B base models.On a 30B model with the exact same architecture as our 750B base, we ran a controlled iso-parameter comparison. With identical parameter counts and only ~10% more total training compute, the looped version showed clear gains:| Benchmark | Baseline | + Loop | |---|---|---| | AIME25 | 19.17 | 30.42 | | GPQA-Diamond | 47.58 | 56.26 | | AA-LCR | 40.33 | 47.67 | | MMLU-Pro | 71.65 | 75.05 | | IFBench | 50.20 | 53.47 |

(Evaluated on the 30B model after 200K long-context SFT, with thinking mode enabled.)Two findings stand out:

Longer reasoning chains benefit more. The largest gains show up in math, scientific reasoning, and long-context tasks, which are core to Generalized Coding.

Fewer tokens spent on thinking. Across most benchmarks like GPQA-Diamond and MMLU-Pro, average output length drops by 10–14%, mostly from shorter chains of thought. In effect, part of the reasoning shifts from explicit output tokens into the implicit depth of the loop.

Inference Efficiency

GLM-5.4 reaches up to 200 tokens/s during off-peak hours and maintains 70–80 tokens/s at peak load. Achieving this throughput with a multi-pass Loop architecture required close co-design between the model and our inference infrastructure. Alongside the memory and retrieval savings from our KV cache and sparse index designs, we fused core kernels at the systems level to cut down intermediate memory reads and writes, eliminating the fragmented overhead amplified by looping.

Generalized Coding

Coding has become the foundation for extending model capabilities. Since going all-in on coding in early 2025, we have unlocked Agentic Engineering, Long-Horizon Tasks, and Cybersecurity. Now we are pushing toward Generalized Coding. It has a higher ceiling and broader impact, and GLM-5.4 is just the starting point.Driven by improvements in both coding and vision, GLM-5.4 generalizes well beyond traditional software development. # Z.ai’s GLM-5.4 runs its layers twice to rival 2T-parameter models

The Chinese lab runs 28 layers of its base model twice instead of adding parameters. Coding Plan subscribers get it first, with API access and open weights promised after safety checks.

Z.ai has released GLM-5.4, its first flagship model built on a Loop Transformer. The design runs some of the model’s layers more than once. The Chinese lab, also known as Zhipu AI, published a technical blog on 23 November. It said the model matches the intelligence of models with 2 to 3 trillion parameters.

GLM-5.4 works at the 750-billion-parameter scale. It is out now for subscribers to Z.ai’s GLM Coding Plan, in its ZCode tool and in Z.ai Chat. API access will follow a safety evaluation. Z.ai plans to release the open weights after safety hardening.

Introducing GLM-5.4: Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer.

– Loops existing layers in the GLM-5 base model for deeper reasoning

– Pushes beyond traditional coding to video, games, 3D shaders, and CAD modeling

– Adds vision capabilities for stronger visual coding
API access will open after safety evaluation. Model weights will be released responsibly.

Z.ai (@Zai_org) November 23, 2026

## Looping instead of growing

In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per pass. GLM-5.4 runs 28 layers of the GLM-5 base model twice. That gives a deeper network with no extra parameters. The idea dates back to the 2018 Universal Transformer, Z.ai said. Thinking Machines released a looped model for laptops last week.

Looped models trained from scratch still trail standard ones on the same compute budget, according to Z.ai. So it adapted its already trained base model through continued training. To keep costs down, the second pass reuses the first pass’s cache and attention indices. It adds only a small sliding window of its own.

Z.ai tested the design on 1B, 4B, 30B and 750B base models. On the 30B model, looping used about 10% more training compute. It brought the biggest gains in maths, scientific reasoning and long-context tasks, the company said. Average output length on benchmarks such as GPQA-Diamond and MMLU-Pro fell by 10% to 14%.

Z.ai did not publish benchmark scores for GLM-5.4 itself. It said the model reaches up to 200 tokens a second off-peak and 70 to 80 at peak load.

## Beyond software

Z.ai calls the release the start of “Generalized Coding”, where code becomes the basis for a wider range of tasks. Its demos include a music video the model narrated itself and a complete game. Others show a 3D scene built with custom shaders and a 6-axis robotic arm modelled in FreeCAD.

The company named one limitation: the model tends to get caught in overly long “marathon thinking” loops. Z.ai said that extra self-correction still improves accuracy.

GLM-5.4 is now available to all GLM Coding Plan users.

New vision capabilities and stronger all-round coding performance.

For users with weekly quotas, GLM-5.4 now comes with 50% more quota compared to GLM-5.3.

Zixuan Li (@ZixuanLi_) November 23, 2026

The previous model, GLM-5.3, focused on coding and cybersecurity. Anthropic said in October that it nearly matched Mythos at cyber exploits. Z.ai and Concordia AI have also proposed six stages for managing the risks of open-weight models.

Z.ai said a significantly larger model is coming soon.

GLM-5.4 Launched — 2026-11-23

# GLM 5.4

GLM-5.4 is Z.ai's first flagship Loop Transformer model, released 2026-11-23. It is available today via GLM Coding Plan, ZCode, and Z.ai Chat — with standard API access coming soon.

## Create with GLM 5

## What Is GLM 5.4?

GLM-5.4 is the first flagship model built on Z.ai's Loop Transformer architecture — the same GLM-5 base, but with 28 layers looped twice for deeper reasoning without adding parameters. Z.ai says it reaches intelligence comparable to 2T–3T parameter models.

01

### Loop Transformer: depth without scale

Instead of adding more parameters, GLM-5.4 loops 28 weight-shared layers of the GLM-5 base model for two iterations per forward pass. Z.ai says it reaches intelligence comparable to 2T–3T parameter models — at 750B total parameters.

02

### Vision + Generalized Coding

GLM-5.4 adds new vision capabilities alongside its coding improvements. Z.ai has demonstrated it generating and editing videos, building complete games, CAD modeling in FreeCAD, and creating interactive 3D scenes from GLSL shaders.

03

### An independent service, not Z.ai official

glm5.app is an independent third-party service. GLM 5.4 is not yet available here — the models you can chat with on this site are GLM 5.3 (default) and GLM 5.3 Flash. This page tracks the official GLM-5.4 release for your reference.

Release Status

## GLM 5.4 Release Status: What Z.ai Has and Hasn't Confirmed

Verified facts from the official Z.ai blog and docs as of 2026-11-23.

01

### ✅ Released — 2026-11-23

Z.ai officially announced GLM-5.4 on 2026-11-23. It is available today via GLM Coding Plan (z.ai/subscribe), ZCode (zcode.z.ai), and Z.ai Chat (chat.z.ai).

02

### ✅ Architecture confirmed

Loop Transformer: 28 GLM-5 base layers, looped twice per forward pass. 750B parameter scale. Z.ai says intelligence is comparable to 2T–3T parameter models.

03

### ⏳ Standard API — coming soon

Z.ai has flagged the standard API as "Coming Soon" at z.ai/model-api. The API will be released after safety hardening is complete. No API pricing has been published.

04

### ⏳ Open weights — planned, no date

Z.ai plans to open-source the weights "responsibly" after safety hardening. As of 2026-11-23, no weights are on Hugging Face and no release date has been set.

05

### ❌ No benchmarks published

Z.ai has not published a benchmark table for the GLM-5.4 flagship. The blog shows a 30B iso-parameter ablation — that is not GLM-5.4's score.

06

### ❌ Not on OpenRouter

As of 2026-11-23, GLM-5.4 is not listed on OpenRouter. Available Z.ai models on OpenRouter include glm-5.3, glm-5.3-flash, glm-5.3-flashx, and glm-5.3-prime.

## GLM 5.4 vs GLM 5.3

Official differences confirmed by Z.ai. All figures from docs.z.ai and z.ai/blog.

GLM-5.4 (new)

### GLM 5.4

How to Use

## How to Use GLM 5.4 Today

Three official entry points from Z.ai. Standard API access is coming soon.

01

01

### Option 1 — Z.ai Chat

Go to chat.z.ai and select GLM-5.4 as your model. This is the quickest way to try GLM-5.4 with no setup — sign in with your Z.ai account and start a conversation.

02

02

### Option 2 — ZCode (AI coding environment)

Open zcode.z.ai for a dedicated coding environment powered by GLM-5.4. ZCode is designed for software engineering tasks, file edits, and multi-step coding projects. GLM-5.4 is also available on Trae, WorkBuddy, Qoder, and OpenCode.

03

03

### Option 3 — GLM Coding Plan + your own tools

Subscribe to GLM Coding Plan at z.ai/subscribe (from $18/month; China users: bigmodel.cn/glm-coding). In Claude Code, set the model to glm-5.4[1m] — the [1m] suffix selects 1M-context mode as designed by Z.ai. For other tools, use model ID glm-5.4 with the endpoint https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4.

04

04

### Step 4 — Test with real tasks

No benchmarks have been published for GLM-5.4. We recommend testing with your own real-world tasks. Note that Z.ai acknowledges the model can get caught in overly long "marathon thinking" loops on complex problems — keep an eye on response length when testing.

## Can I Use GLM 5.4 on glm5.app?

Not yet. GLM 5.4 is not currently available on this site.

01

### GLM 5.4 is not on glm5.app

glm5.app is an independent third-party service. The model GLM-5.4 is not in our model catalog. If you send "model": "glm-5.4" to our API, it returns a 404 model_not_found error.

02

### GLM 5.3 is available (default)

The default chat model on glm5.app is GLM 5.3 (API ID: glm-5.3). Plus and Enterprise subscribers can use GLM 5.3 without spending credits. Free accounts can try GLM 5.3 using welcome credits.

03

### GLM 5.3 Flash — free daily messages

GLM 5.3 Flash (API ID: glm-5.3-flash) supports image input and gives free accounts a daily free message quota at no credit cost. It's the best option for getting started without a subscription.

## GLM 5.4 FAQ

Answers to the questions we see most often about GLM-5.4.

## 

### What is the GLM 5.4 release date?

GLM-5.4 was released on 2026-11-23. Z.ai lead Zixuan Li announced it on X, and the official Z.ai blog published the technical overview the same day.

## 

### Is GLM-5.4 available via API, and what does it cost?

The standard GLM-5.4 API is marked "Coming Soon" on z.ai/model-api. Z.ai says it will be released after safety hardening. No API pricing has been announced. The only current programmatic access is through the GLM Coding Plan endpoint at https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4.

## 

### What are GLM-5.4's benchmark scores?

Z.ai has not published a benchmark table for the GLM-5.4 flagship. Z.ai says in an internal evaluation across 200 real-world coding scenarios the model performed strongly on visual coding, visual replication, and long-horizon tasks — but no scores were published. The official blog also includes a 30B iso-parameter ablation, but that is a small-model experiment, not a GLM-5.4 score.

## 

### Is GLM 5.4 open-weight? Can I download it on Hugging Face?

Not yet. Z.ai plans to open-source the GLM-5.4 weights "responsibly after completing necessary safety hardening" — but no release date has been set. As of 2026-11-23, Hugging Face's latest GLM-5 weights are still GLM-5.3.

## 

### Is GLM-5.4 on OpenRouter?

No. As of 2026-11-23, GLM-5.4 does not appear in the OpenRouter model list. Available Z.ai models on OpenRouter include glm-5.3, glm-5.3-flash, glm-5.3-flashx, and glm-5.3-prime.

## 

### Is there a GLM-5.4-Flash or GLM-5.4-Air model?

No. Z.ai has not announced a GLM-5.4-Flash or GLM-5.4-Air. The current fast-inference option in the GLM Coding Plan is GLM-5.3-Flash. The only GLM-5.4 model available is the full 750B flagship.

## 

### Can I use GLM 5.4 for free?

GLM-5.4 is not currently available on glm5.app. To access it today, you need a Z.ai account via chat.z.ai, ZCode at zcode.z.ai, or a GLM Coding Plan subscription (from $18/month) for API access. If you want a free coding AI on this site, GLM 5.3 Flash gives free accounts a daily free message quota.

## 

### Does GLM 5.4 support vision / image input?

Yes. Vision is a new capability added in GLM-5.4 — Z.ai's official announcement explicitly highlights "new vision capabilities." The model can process images and generate visual code (3D scenes, game graphics). On glm5.app, GLM 5.3 Flash already supports image input as the available multimodal option.

## 

### Is glm5.app the official GLM or Z.ai website?

No. glm5.app is an independent third-party service. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by Zhipu AI or Z.ai Inc. For official Z.ai products, visit z.ai, chat.z.ai, or zcode.z.ai.

## 

### How does the Loop Transformer in GLM 5.4 work?

Instead of stacking more layers (which requires more parameters), GLM-5.4 loops a shared block of 28 GLM-5 base layers for two iterations per forward pass. Each pass refines the hidden states from the previous one — effectively giving the model deeper reasoning without increasing its parameter count. Z.ai says this lets the 750B model reach intelligence comparable to 2T–3T parameter models. The main tradeoff is that it can fall into overly long "marathon thinking" loops on complex problems.

Start here

## Try GLM 5.3 While You Wait for GLM 5.4

GLM 5.4 is not yet on glm5.app. The best available option here is GLM 5.3 — the previous flagship — plus GLM 5.3 Flash for free daily messages and image input.

# Moonshot AI Kimi K2.6 now available on Workers AI

@cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 is now available on Workers AI, in partnership with Moonshot AI for Day 0 support. Kimi K2.6 is a native multimodal agentic model from Moonshot AI that advances practical capabilities in long-horizon coding, coding-driven design, proactive autonomous execution, and swarm-based task orchestration.

Built on a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with 1T total parameters and 32B active per token, Kimi K2.6 delivers frontier-scale intelligence with efficient inference. It scores competitively against GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6 on agentic and coding benchmarks, including BrowseComp (83.2), SWE-Bench Verified (80.2), and Terminal-Bench 2.0 (66.7).

## Key capabilities

- 262.1k token context window for retaining full conversation history, tool definitions, and codebases across long-running agent sessions
- Long-horizon coding with significant improvements on complex, end-to-end coding tasks across languages including Rust, Go, and Python
- Coding-driven design that transforms simple prompts and visual inputs into production-ready interfaces and full-stack workflows
- Agent swarm orchestration scaling horizontally to 300 sub-agents executing 4,000 coordinated steps for complex autonomous tasks
- Vision inputs for processing images alongside text
- Thinking mode with configurable reasoning depth
- Multi-turn tool calling for building agents that invoke tools across multiple conversation turns

## Differences from Kimi K2.5

If you are migrating from Kimi K2.5, note the following API changes:

- K2.6 useschat_template_kwargs.thinking to control reasoning, replacing chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking
- K2.6 returns reasoning content in thereasoning field, replacing reasoning_content

## Get started

Use Kimi K2.6 through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()), the REST API at /ai/run, or the OpenAI-compatible endpoint at /v1/chat/completions. You can also use AI Gateway with any of these endpoints.

For more information, refer to the Kimi K2.6 model page and pricing.

Kimi.title: Kimi API: model IDs, thinking toggle, web search, and Claude Code
Kimi.description: Moonshot AI’s Kimi models, including Kimi K3, K2.6, and the coding-focused K2.7 Code. ... Kimi models are provided by Moonshot AI directly (moonshot), and some models also have providers such as Azure AI Foundry and Alibaba Cloud Model Studio...
Kimi.content:
Opens a sub-menu

# Kimi family

Moonshot AI’s Kimi models, including Kimi K3, K2.6, and the coding-focused K2.7 Code. Called through the OpenAI-compatible API; the Anthropic native API is also supported, so they can be used in Claude Code.

## Common tasks

## Models

For the full model list and live prices, see the models page . Model IDs have the prefixmoonshotai/, which can be omitted.

Common model IDs (copy them exactly)

Kimi K3
moonshotai/kimi-k31M context, supports image input
Kimi K2.6
moonshotai/kimi-k2.6256K context, supports image input
Kimi K2.7 Code
moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-codeFor coding
Kimi models are provided by Moonshot AI directly (moonshot), and some models also have providers such as Azure AI Foundry and Alibaba Cloud Model Studio; the provider is selected automatically by default. To specify one, see Provider routing.

## Examples

### Python

kimi_basic.py
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.ofox.ai/v1", api_key=os.environ["OFOX_API_KEY"])

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="moonshotai/kimi-k3",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain idempotency in one sentence."}],
    extra_body={"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}},
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

## Thinking mode

Key pointKimi has thinking on by default. When you do not need it, set the thinking type to disabled (except for K2.7 Code HighSpeed).

Model | Default | Turning off thinking 
---|---|---
Kimi K3, K2.6, K2.7 Code | On | "thinking": {"type": "disabled"} 
Kimi K2.7 Code HighSpeed | On | Not supported; passing disabled returns 400 

Measured on the same math problem: Kimi K3 took about 30 seconds by default and about 3 seconds with thinking off; K2.6 used about 11,000 thinking tokens and took about 4.5 minutes by default, and about 40 seconds with thinking off. Thinking tokens are billed at the output rate, and their count is inusage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens.

Reading thinking content: in streaming responses it is indelta.reasoning_content; in non-streaming responses it is in message.reasoning_details, where you concatenate the text of each item in order.

## Web search

Addweb_search to tools on the Responses API, and the model searches on its own and attaches cited sources to its answer:

kimi_web_search.py
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.ofox.ai/v1", api_key=os.environ["OFOX_API_KEY"])

resp = client.responses.create(
    model="moonshotai/kimi-k3",
    tools=[{"type": "web_search"}],
    input="What is the latest stable version of Python?",
)
print(resp.output_text)
for item in resp.output:
    if item.type == "message":
        for part in item.content:
            for a in getattr(part, "annotations", None) or []:
                print("Source:", a.title, a.url)
- Supported by Kimi K3 and K2.6 in our tests.output contains reasoning, web_search_call, and message items in that order, and the cited sources are in the annotations of the message content.
- Searches are billed per call; for rates, see the model page .

## Use in Claude Code

Kimi models support the Anthropic native API athttps://api.ofox.ai/anthropic:

Claude Code configuration values

ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
https://api.ofox.ai/anthropic
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKENPaste your OfoxAI API key

ANTHROPIC_MODEL
moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code
When called through the Anthropic API, thinking content is returned asthinking blocks. For the full Claude Code setup steps, see Claude Code setup.

## Image input and structured output

- Kimi K3 and K2.6 support image input using standardimage_url content blocks; see Vision for the format.
- response_format supports json_schema and json_object; tool calling uses the standard tools parameter. See Structured output for the format.
- Repeated request prefixes are cached automatically; the hit count is inusage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens.

## Common errors

HTTP · type | Error message | Cause | Fix 
---|---|---|---
400 invalid_request_error | invalid thinking: only type=enabled is allowed for this model | K2.7 Code HighSpeed does not support turning off thinking | Remove the thinking parameter, or switch to K2.7 Code 
429 rate_limit_error | Rate limit reached for the requested model. Please retry after a short delay. | Too many requests | Retry later; see Rate limits 
404 model_not_found | Model 'moonshotai/kimi-k9' not found | Model ID misspelled, or the moonshot/ prefix was used | The prefix is moonshotai/; copy the model ID from this page 
Request timeout | — | Thinking is on by default, and complex questions take longer | Turn off thinking, use streaming, or set the client timeout to 600 seconds or more 

For other general errors, see Error handling.

## Official docs

## FAQ

How do I write Kimi model IDs?

The standard form is moonshotai/kimi-k3; you can also omit the prefix and write kimi-k3. Writing moonshot/kimi-k3 returns 404.

How do I turn off thinking for Kimi?

Pass "thinking": {"type": "disabled"}; with the OpenAI SDK, put it in extra_body. K2.7 Code HighSpeed does not support turning it off, and passing it returns 400.

Can Kimi search the web?

Yes. Use the Responses API and add {"type": "web_search"} to tools; the answer will include cited sources. Supported by Kimi K3 and K2.6 in our tests.

Can Claude Code use Kimi?

Yes. Set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to https://api.ofox.ai/anthropic and set the model to moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code or moonshotai/kimi-k3.

Why is Kimi K2.6 so slow?

K2.6 has thinking on by default, and complex questions may use more than ten thousand thinking tokens and take several minutes. Turn thinking off when you do not need it, or switch to Kimi K3.

Kimi.title: Kimi K3 and China's Open-Weight Model Wave
Kimi.description: Kimi K3 is Moonshot AI's flagship model for long-horizon coding and agentic work. At 2.8 trillion parameters — a mixture-of-experts design that activates 16 of its 896 experts per token — it is the largest open-weight model announced to date.
Kimi.content:
# Kimi K3 and China's Open-Weight Model Wave

Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 on July 16, and the benchmarks put an open-weight model next to the best closed ones for the first time. The catch is access. K3 sits on Moonshot's platform, GLM-5.2 on Z.ai's, DeepSeek V4 Pro on DeepSeek's, MiniMax M3 on MiniMax's — four accounts, four billing relationships, four API dashboards, all before you have written a line of code.

LLM Gateway routes every one of them through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint. One key, one bill, and a switch between Kimi K3 and any of 200+ models is a one-word change to your request.

## What is Kimi K3?

Kimi K3 is Moonshot AI's flagship model for long-horizon coding and agentic work. At 2.8 trillion parameters — a mixture-of-experts design that activates 16 of its 896 experts per token — it is the largest open-weight model announced to date. Moonshot published the full weights on July 26, 2026, a day ahead of its own deadline — see what the open-weight release actually lets you do.

The specs that matter in practice:

- 1M-token context window (1,048,576 tokens), with output configurable up to the same 1M — enough to hold a large repository plus its docs in a single request
- Always-on reasoning — K3 thinks before every answer; there is no non-thinking mode
- Vision, tool calls, and JSON output supported out of the box
- Prompt caching at a 90% discount on repeated input

Early results back up the size. K3 ranks fourth of 189 models on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — level with Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 — and took first place in Arena's Frontend Code evaluation in blind developer testing. It posted 93.5% on GPQA Diamond and 88.3% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, the strongest open-weight results published on both at release.

## Kimi K3 pricing

Through LLM Gateway you pay Moonshot's published per-token rates:

Tokens | Price per million 
---|---
Input | $3.00 
Cached input | $0.30 
Output | $15.00 

The cached-input rate is the number to watch. Coding agents re-send the same system prompt, file context, and conversation history on every step, so in a long agent session most of your input tokens are cache hits billed at a tenth of the fresh rate.

## The open-weight wave K3 leads

K3 is the headline, but 2026 has produced a full roster of frontier-class open-weight models from Chinese labs — most MIT-licensed (K3 ships under its own custom license), all available through LLM Gateway at provider list prices:

Model | Lab | Released | Context | Input $/M | Output $/M 
---|---|---|---|---|---
Kimi K3 | Moonshot AI | Jul 2026 | 1M | $3.00 | $15.00 
GLM-5.2 | Z.ai | Jun 2026 | 1M | $1.40 | $4.40 
MiniMax M3 | MiniMax | Jun 2026 | 512K | $0.60 | $2.40 
DeepSeek V4 Pro | DeepSeek | Apr 2026 | 1M | $0.435 | $0.87 

Each fills a different slot. GLM-5.2 (744B, MIT license) was the top-ranked open model before K3 arrived — its output costs under a third of K3's rate ($4.40 vs $15.00 per million) and its input about 47% ($1.40 vs $3.00). DeepSeek V4 Pro (1.6T total, 49B active, MIT license) delivers a 1M-token context at under a dollar per million output tokens. MiniMax M3 is the multimodal option, taking image input alongside text. And if you want the cheapest entry point,mimo-v2.5 runs through the same endpoint from $0.14/M input and $0.28/M output.

## One endpoint for all of them

LLM Gateway speaks the OpenAI API, so anything that can call OpenAI can call Kimi K3:
curl https://api.llmgateway.io/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LLM_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "kimi-k3",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Refactor this module to remove the circular import."}]
  }'

Swapping to GLM-5.2 or DeepSeek V4 Pro is a change to themodel field — no new SDK, no new key. If you need a specific upstream, pin it with the provider prefix (moonshot/kimi-k3); otherwise the gateway routes to a healthy provider and fails over automatically if one goes down. Kimi K3 is served by both Moonshot and Novita, so a single-provider outage does not take your app with it.

Every request lands in the same dashboard: per-model cost, token counts, cache-hit rates, and latency, across all providers.

## Run Kimi K3 on a flat rate with DevPass

If K3 is headed for your coding agent, the cheapest way to run it hard is DevPass — a flat monthly plan that works with Claude Code, OpenCode, Cline, Cursor (plan and agent mode), and anything else OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible:

Plan | Price | Model usage included 
---|---|---
Lite | $29/mo | $58 at provider rates 
Pro | $79/mo | $158 
Max | $179/mo | $358 

Every dollar of allowance is metered at the provider rates above, so on Pro you get $158 of model usage for $79 — and a runaway agent loop cannot produce a surprise invoice.

One gating detail to know: at $15 per million output tokens, Kimi K3 counts as a premium-tier model on DevPass, so it draws from a weekly premium allowance — roughly $5.80 per week of premium usage on Lite, $19 on Pro, and $54 on Max, drawn from your monthly pool. GLM-5.2, MiniMax M3, and DeepSeek V4 Pro are all standard-tier: no weekly cap, usable until your monthly allowance runs out. A workable pattern is K3 for the hardest tasks and GLM-5.2 or DeepSeek V4 Pro for the bulk of the loop. If you burn through the premium allowance mid-week, a Reset Pass restores it instantly — Max includes two per cycle, and extra passes are $5 on Lite, $15 on Pro and $45 on Max.

## Or pay as you go

For production apps, PAYG credits skip the subscription entirely. Top up from $10, pay each provider's published per-token price as you go, and LLM Gateway adds a flat 5% platform fee at top-up — the per-token rates themselves are pass-through. You keep the same single endpoint, automatic failover, prompt caching, and cost dashboard, metered to the token.

The two models work together: DevPass for your own coding agents, PAYG for the product you ship.

## Getting started

- Try LLM Gateway free — one key for Kimi K3 and 200+ other models
- Get DevPass — flat-rate plans from $29/mo for coding agents
- Read the Kimi K3 API guide or see how the plans compare in 10 Best AI Coding Plans in 2026
- Go deeper: the open-weights release, Kimi K3 vs Claude Opus 4.8, and the full open-source LLM ranking

xAI.content:
## Oregon Department of Justice

# Media

### Department Communications and General Information

Choose to search: or

# Oregon Attorney General Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones Hold Grok Accountable for Failing to Block Child Exploitation

November 23, 2026
• Posted in Homepage, Lawsuits and Letters, Media Release 

## Oregon and Virginia take legal actions against Grok and seek significant new protections

As part of his ongoing Keeping Kids Safe Initiative, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield today took steps to bring accountability to the operators of the X social media platform and its Grok AI assistant for promoting both products as safe while failing to prevent Grok from generating sexualized images of people without their consent, including child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

X and Grok are products of Elon Musk’s SpaceX corporation; the AI and social media subsidiaries are referred to as xAI. Today’s lawsuit was filed in collaboration with Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones, who filed a separate but similar action.

“SpaceX allowed Grok and the X platform to create, host, and share unacceptable and dangerous content—and in fact knowingly designed a product without the obviously necessary safeguards in place,” said Attorney General Rayfield. “It’s no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material. The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug, which they promoted as ‘spicy mode.’”

“Today’s lawsuit is about seeking justice for the millions of Virginians who maintain accounts on X and were misled by the company’s false reassurances that their data and images would be safe on the platform,” said Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones. “When xAI allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they not only prioritized growth and engagement over safety, but they deceived the public about it.”

In their filings, the Attorney Generals show that xAI marketed Grok as an AI companion with a “rebellious streak,” knowing that its video and image generation technology would be used to produce CSAM, non-consensual intimate images of adults and children (NCII), and other sexualized imagery. The companies prioritized growth and engagement over safety by weakening industry-standard safeguards, promoting Grok’s ability to generate sexualized content, and enabling the widespread creation and distribution of sexualized images through Grok’s integration with X.

In fact, xAI created and promoted a “spicy mode” that specifically allowed for the creation of nude and otherwise sexualized images.

A study by the Center for Countering Digital Harm (“CCDH”) estimated that, between December 29, 2025, and January 8, 2026, Grok created and posted on X approximately three million sexualized images, including approximately 23,000 images that appeared to depict children. That’s an average pace of roughly 190 sexualized images per minute, and one sexualized image of a child approximately every 41 seconds. Nearly 30% of the sexualized images of children identified by CCDH in its study remained publicly accessible in posts on X a week or more after they were identified—and even many of those that were “removed” could still be accessed via separate URLs.

xAI publicly assured consumers that robust protections were in place to prevent Grok from creating CSAM, NCII, and other sexualized images, but millions of people—including in Oregon and Virginia—were nevertheless exposed to harmful content and the risk that their own images could be manipulated into sexually explicit content without their consent.

“Time and again, xAI and X told consumers they were being protected from abuses. That was false. Instead, the tool permitted users to routinely create and circulate non-consensual intimate imagery and sexualized images, and child sexual abuse material (CSAM), causing harm to individuals and children,” added AG Jones. “Companies that deploy powerful tools don’t get to ignore consumer safety and call it innovation. The law applies to everyone, and this office will hold big tech accountable when they break the law.”

“Like the other technology companies that we’re holding accountable, xAI not only knowingly endangered kids and our communities, but they also lied to our faces about non-existent safety measures,” added AG Rayfield.

Last week, AG Rayfield launched the Oregon Department of Justice’s Keeping Kids Safe Initiative, including legal actions and investigations against social media and AI companies for harming kids and misleading parents and the public about the safety of their platforms.

AG Rayfield’s lawsuit was filed in Multnomah County Circuit Court. Attorney General Jones’ lawsuit was filed in the Circuit Court for the City of Richmond.

RICHMOND, Va. – Today, Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones took a significant step in holding operators of X and its AI tool, Grok, accountable for knowingly failing to protect Virginians, while falsely promoting the safety of its platform and AI tool.

In the lawsuit, the Commonwealth of Virginia alleges that SpaceX, the telecommunications and space transportation conglomerate that operates the social network X and its artificial intelligence company, xAI (now called “SpaceX Super Intelligence”), and developed the Grok family of large language models, failed to prevent Grok from generating sexualized images of people, including children, without their knowledge or consent—while simultaneously promoting the safety of the social media platform and AI tool. The Grok-generated content includes non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII), other non-consensual sexualized images, and Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM). Today’s suit was filed in collaboration with Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield, who filed a separate but similar action.

“This lawsuit is about seeking justice for the millions of Virginians who maintain accounts on X and were misled by the company’s false reassurances that their data and images would be safe on the platform,” said Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones. “When xAI allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it. Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this company accountable.”

With a single existing photograph, Grok could, and did, fabricate a realistic image or video of a person nude, or partially nude, or engaged in sexual activity, all without the individual’s knowledge or consent. This violation is not acceptable.

The company ignored industry-standard safeguards so xAI could distinguish itself in the AI arms race. Grok’s ability to generate sexualized content was leveraged as a promotional opportunity. These exploitations of Virginian’s safety enabled the widespread creation and distribution of sexualized images through Grok’s integration with X.

“SpaceX allowed Grok and the X platform to create, host, and share unacceptable and dangerous content—and in fact knowingly designed a product without the obviously necessary safeguards in place,” said Attorney General Rayfield. “It’s no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material. The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug, which they promoted as ‘spicy mode.’”

In his filing, Attorney General Jones shows that SpaceX and its subsidiaries marketed Grok as an AI companion with a “rebellious streak,” knowing that its video and image generation technology would be used to produce CSAM, non-consensual intimate images of adults and children (NCII), and other sexualized imagery. In fact, X and its subsidiaries created and promoted a “spicy mode” that specifically allowed for the creation of nude and otherwise sexualized images.

A study by the Center for Countering Digital Harm (“CCDH”) estimated that, between December 29, 2025, and January 8, 2026, Grok created and posted on X approximately three million sexualized images, including approximately 23,000 images that appeared to depict children. That’s an average pace of roughly 190 sexualized images per minute, and one sexualized image of a child approximately every 41 seconds. Nearly 30% of the sexualized images of children identified by CCDH in its study remained publicly accessible in posts on X a week or more after they were identified—and even many of those that were “removed” could still be accessed via separate URLs.

SpaceX and its subsidiaries publicly assured consumers that robust protections were in place to prevent Grok from creating CSAM, NCII, and other sexualized images. In reality, millions of people — including in Oregon and Virginia — were nevertheless exposed to harmful content and the risk that their own images could be manipulated into sexually explicit content without their consent.

“Time and again, xAI and X told consumers they were being protected from abuses. That was false. Instead, the tool permitted users to routinely create and circulate non-consensual intimate imagery and sexualized images, and child sexual abuse material (CSAM), causing harm to individuals and children,” added Attorney General Jones. “Companies that deploy powerful tools don’t get to ignore consumer safety and call it innovation. The law applies to everyone, and this office will hold big tech accountable when they break the law.”

“Like the other technology companies that we’re holding accountable, xAI not only knowingly endangered kids and our communities, but they also lied to our faces about non-existent safety measures,” added Attorney General Rayfield.

Attorney General Jones’ lawsuit was filed in the Circuit Court for the City of Richmond. Attorney General Rayfield’s lawsuit was filed in Multnomah County Circuit Court.

Published on: November 23, 2026

# Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok’s porn deepfakes

State AGs called the weak safeguards built into Elon Musk’s AI image generator ‘not a failure but a feature.’

State AGs called the weak safeguards built into Elon Musk’s AI image generator ‘not a failure but a feature.’

Jess Weatherbed is a news writer focused on creative industries, computing, and internet culture. Jess started her career at TechRadar, covering news and hardware reviews.

In separate but similar lawsuits filed on Monday, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones accused SpaceX of violating state consumer protection laws by ignoring industry-standard safeguards and falsely promoting the safety of its X social media platform and Grok AI features. The complaint filed in Virginia accuses Musk of willfully ignoring growing concerns around AI-generated sexualized deepfakes, and “instead saw a market opportunity for more profits,” describing the weak safeguards around Grok as “not a failure but a feature.”

“Time and again, xAI and X told consumers they were being protected from abuses. That was false. Instead, the tool permitted users to routinely create and circulate non-consensual intimate imagery and sexualized images, and child sexual abuse material (CSAM), causing harm to individuals and children,” Jones said in a press statement. “Companies that deploy powerful tools don’t get to ignore consumer safety and call it innovation.”

The complaints largely center around Grok Imagine, a tool that allows Grok and X users to generate images and videos. In August 2025, Grok maker xAI (which Musk has since merged with SpaceX) launched a “spicy” mode for Grok Imagine that spat out sexualized content including nude deepfakes of celebrities like Taylor Swift. In January 2026, Grok gained a feature that allowed X users to instantly edit any image without requiring consent from the original poster — resulting in X becoming flooded with nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes of adults and minors.

xAI made several changes to restrict access to Grok image editing, moving some capabilities behind a paywall and blocking certain requests for sexual poses, swimwear, or explicit scenarios. Our testing at the Verge following these restriction updates found they did little to prevent the bot from creating sexualized deepfakes, however.

Both of the Oregon and Virginia lawsuits are seeking financial damages.

The X Safety team said in a statement released after the lawsuits were announced that it takes appropriate measures to address users who generate sexual content involving minors:

To stay ahead of this disgusting and indefensible conduct, we keep testing and adjusting those protections as these abusers change tactics. xAI.content:
# Virginia, Oregon sue SpaceX over AI deepfake porn, child sexual abuse material

Virginia and Oregon’s attorneys general announced on Monday separate lawsuits against SpaceX for allegedly creating and promoting AI deepfake pornography and sexually explicit photos of children.

Virginia’s lawsuit accused SpaceX of failing to prevent its AI chatbot, Grok, “from generating sexualized images of people, including children, without their knowledge or consent.”

The lawsuits referenced marketing where xAI, which SpaceX acquired in February, advertised Grok as an AI companion with a “rebellious streak” that would “answer spicy questions that are rejected by most other AI systems.”

“When xAI allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it,” Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones (D) said in a statement.

Jones called out Grok Imagine’s “spicy mode,” which is accused of allowing users to specifically create “nude and otherwise sexualized images.”

One study mentioned in the cases, by the Center for Countering Digital Harm, found the Grok account on the social platform X reportedly posted about 3 million sexualized images, including about 23,000 images that appeared to depict children, between Dec. 29 and Jan. 8.

“It’s no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material,” Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield (D) said in a statement. “Like the other technology companies that we’re holding accountable, xAI not only knowingly endangered kids and our communities, but they also lied to our faces about non-existent safety measures.”

On Monday, X Safety wrote, “Sexual content involving minors, whether real or AI-generated, is abhorrent. It has no place on X or in Grok, and neither do explicit images of real people made without their consent.”

When “bad actors found ways to misuse Grok Imagine,” the company said it acted quickly to “tighten its protections, the statement continued.

“We will continue to work with the authorities via all available means to pursue these bad actors,” it concluded.

The dual lawsuits come after Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) and media personality Paris Hilton held a press conference last week to push for the passage of the Defiance Act, a bill that would give victims a civil right of action to sue over deepfake pornography.

It already passed the Senate but is facing headwinds in the House during the lame-duck session.

SpaceX did not respond immediately to The Hill’s request for comment.
